quest:102.text: Patrolling Westfall. Gnoll packs roam Westfall's grasslands, threatening the people who still live there. Captain Danuvin calls on volunteers from Sentinel Hill to hunt them, fearing they work with the thieves in the Deadmines. Sentinel Hill is Westfall's main defense, held by local volunteers rather than royal troops. With Stormwind sending no soldiers to protect the outer farmlands, the people formed the People's Militia. Captain Danuvin, once a farmer in Westfall, leads them and refuses to abandon his homeland. The militia depends on travelers who pass through to help hold its perimeter against the dangers gathering across the plains. Gnolls now threaten the refugees and squatters struggling to survive in Westfall. Danuvin's scouts believe the packs are working with bandits based in the Deadmines. He sends hunters to collect gnoll paws, hoping to curb the packs' growing patrols and break any cooperation between the beasts and the outlaws.

quest:103.text: Keeper of the Flame. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the coast. The spectral sailor seeks oil to keep the beacon burning after murlocs killed the living keepers, so ships can pass the reefs safely. Westfall Lighthouse stands on a rocky islet off the zone’s southwest shore, where its light once guided sailors through the Great Sea’s shallow waters. That duty ended when Old Murk-Eye led a murloc attack and killed the keeper and his family. Captain Grayson, a sailor who died in the waters by these rocks, now watches over the tower as a ghost. Death left him unable to stop the slaughter, but he will not let the lighthouse go dark. No living keeper remains to tend the flame, so Captain Grayson needs an unusual fuel. The rogue Harvest Watchers roaming Westfall’s abandoned farmlands carry flasks of machinery oil inside their rusted bodies. Grayson sends you ashore to recover the oil from these broken constructs. With it, the beacon can keep burning and guide other captains past the reefs.

quest:109.text: Report to Gryan Stoutmantle. Westfall needs fighters, and Report to Gryan Stoutmantle sends you to answer the call. The crown leaves the outer farmlands to fend for themselves, so local defenders gather under Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Westfall calls for skilled fighters from across the river. Brigands, gnolls, and hostile harvest golems are driving the farmlands into chaos. With no royal battalions answering, local volunteers must defend the realm. The road leads you to Gryan Stoutmantle in the stone tower atop Sentinel Hill. He leads the People's Militia, a force of farmers, retired veterans, and mercenaries formed in response to royal inaction. The farmlands face a bitter guerrilla war against lawlessness.

quest:1097.text: Elmore's Task. Smith Argus sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind to help Grimand Elmore. The dwarven weaponsmith needs help with a delivery bound for his kin in Khaz Modan, and Argus trusts you to make the journey. In Goldshire, blacksmith Smith Argus watches for travelers he can trust with work beyond clearing wolves and kobolds. Grimand Elmore, a skilled dwarven weaponsmith in Stormwind, has asked for help with a delivery to his kin in Khaz Modan. Argus sees you as fit for the journey and sends you toward the city gates to answer Elmore's call. Stormwind and Ironforge depend on open trade and goodwill to keep both realms supplied and united. Argus says Elwynn Forest needs defenders, but honoring promises to the dwarves matters too. In northeastern Stormwind, the Dwarven District leads you to Elmore's shop, where a journey beyond the forest begins.

quest:1099.text: Goblins Win!. In Thousand Needles, a goblin race ticket pays off when the goblins come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The goblin race ticket is the stub that counts when the goblins win. Hold on to it, and a goblin prize box is yours once the result is in. The gnome ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

quest:111.text: Speak with Gramma. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks Gramma Stonefield's help to meet Maybell Maclure. Their families' bitter feud keeps the young lovers apart, and Tommy Joe hopes his grandmother can find a way for them to see each other. Tommy Joe Stonefield and Maybell Maclure keep their romance secret from their feuding families. The Stonefields and Maclures have fought over their farms for years, making their neighboring homesteads hostile ground. Tommy Joe wants to meet Maybell without provoking violence between their kin, so he turns to his grandmother for help. Gramma Stonefield stays indoors, but she knows the feud well. She understands that the families cannot truly unite while their bad blood remains. Still, she will not let their grudge crush young love. Rather than urge caution, Gramma begins looking for small chances to bring Tommy Joe and Maybell together.

quest:112.text: Collecting Kelp. In Goldshire, Maybell Maclure seeks a way to visit Tommy Joe Stonefield unseen. William Pestle needs rare crystal kelp to brew an invisibility liquor for her. The feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families keeps Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield from meeting openly. Maybell wants to see her beloved without provoking an armed clash between their kin, so she seeks a way to cross the valley unseen. William Pestle, an herbalist and apothecary at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, plans to brew an invisibility liquor. The rare ingredients he needs are not in the inn's cupboards. Crystal kelp is the catalyst William Pestle needs for his brew. The fronds usually grow far out in saltwater oceans, but tribal murlocs have carried stashes inland to their crude camps along Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. Their peculiar instincts have led them to haul the marine plants to the freshwater shore. You need to recover enough fronds from the murlocs before returning to Goldshire with them.

quest:114.text: The Escape. Maybell Maclure waits for a way to slip away from her family and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. You bring her William Pestle's Invisibility Liquor, brewed from crystal kelp gathered across the region. The Maclures and Stonefields have feuded for generations, leaving no room for courtship. Gramma Stonefield turns to William Pestle, an alchemist in the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. With crystal kelp from nearby lakes, Pestle brews Invisibility Liquor strong enough to hide Maybell's escape from the Maclure homestead.

quest:117.text: Thunderbrew. In Westfall, Grimbooze Thunderbrew is gathering what he needs for his next batch. Fresh hops keep his ale from turning thick as stew, and he shares kegs with those who help. Grimbooze Thunderbrew keeps his family's brewing tradition alive far from Dun Morogh. Even across Westfall's turbulent plains, he insists on the right ingredients: without proper hops, his current brew may turn into thick stew instead of refreshing ale. Grimbooze celebrates hops, barley, yeast, and malt in cheerful rhymes. With fresh hops, he finishes the fermentation on the spot. Those who supply him receive whole kegs of Thunderbrew Lager, a brew known for its forceful taste.

quest:1174.text: Gnomes Win!. In Thousand Needles, a gnome race ticket pays off when the gnomes come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The gnome race ticket is the stub that counts when the gnomes win. Hold on to it, and a gnome prize box is yours once the result is in. The goblin ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

quest:119.text: Return to Verner. You carry fifty freshly forged horseshoes from Goldshire back to Lakeshire. Smith Argus has finished the order, and Verner Osgood is waiting across the border in Redridge. Smith Argus has forged fifty horseshoes for Lakeshire, and you carry them east from Goldshire. Redridge faces supply shortages and gnoll attacks. The iron shoes help keep horses and draft animals working on its rugged mountain roads. Verner Osgood is relieved when the horseshoes arrive, but Smith Argus has attached a bill to the crate. Verner is annoyed that the Goldshire smith expects payment. Redridge faces pressing dangers, leaving little time to argue over the charge.

quest:12.text: The People's Militia. At Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle tests your mettle for the People's Militia. Stormwind's throne is distracted, and its army is absent, so local volunteers defend Westfall from the Defias Brotherhood. You begin by driving outlaws from the northern fields and mines. Westfall once fed Stormwind, but outlaws, vagrants, and thieves now overrun the region. With the capital sending no royal soldiers to patrol the countryside, Gryan Stoutmantle organized the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill as a local defense force. He calls for decisive action to reclaim Westfall. Anyone seeking the militia's badge must prove they can fight and will protect innocent settlers. Before Stoutmantle trusts new recruits with deeper operations, he sends them against Defias forces near northern homesteads. Defias Trappers and Smugglers work openly near Jangolode Mine, Molsen Farm, and Furlbrow's Pumpkin Patch, pillaging stores and ambushing travelers. You can disrupt their foraging by driving them out, while showing Stoutmantle's scouts that you have the grit for a long fight against crime.

quest:121.text: Messenger to Stormwind. You carry General Marcus Jonathan's reply from Stormwind to Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten the town. The capital offers no troops, leaving the settlement to face danger while Stormwind's leaders delay. You brought Magistrate Solomon's plea for reinforcements to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind. Now you carry his preliminary reply back to Redridge while he waits for approval from the throne. Without royal authorization, the General cannot commit the army. Lakeshire's citizens remain without city guards, and each day brings the settlement closer to falling under the Blackrock clan.

quest:123.text: The Collector. An intercepted dispatch from gnoll raiders in Elwynn Forest lays out when gold shipments leave the abandoned mines. It is addressed to a figure called 'The Collector' and points to an organized operation near Stormwind's garrison. Riverpaw gnoll packs in western Elwynn Forest carry more than furs and crude weapons. Among them, a parchment called the Gold Pickup Schedule lays out dates and times for gold taken from local mines. The intercepted note directs each shipment to an overseer identified only as 'The Collector.' Marshal Dughan hears the news at the Lion's Pride Inn and learns that gold is still being mined and moved. Official mines across Elwynn have been closed for months because of gnoll attacks, kobold infestations, and roaming bandits. Gnolls carrying shipping schedules point to an organized criminal network stealing the kingdom's wealth.

quest:13.text: The People's Militia. Across Westfall, The People's Militia faces a growing Defias threat. Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteers now confront thieves who have moved beyond highway robbery to ransack Moonbrook and the Gold Coast Quarry, and the Militia calls for harsher retaliation. Defias attacks have grown from petty banditry on the roads into a wider threat. Defias Looters and Pillagers, who hurl fire, have overrun Westfall's economic centers. They occupy Moonbrook, strip the Alexston Farmstead, and have taken control of the Gold Coast Quarry. Gryan Stoutmantle sees the danger: if the brigands hold these places, Westfall may become impossible to reclaim without a formal royal army. Stormwind has sent Gryan Stoutmantle no soldiers or supplies, so he calls on the Holy Light and the resolve of Westfall's remaining farmers. The Militia's war of attrition depends on volunteers carrying the fight into Defias strongholds. Driving out the looters will deny the Brotherhood resources and show fearful residents that defenders still fight for Westfall's peace and prosperity.

quest:132.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, The Defias Brotherhood is building a network beyond banditry. Wiley the Black sends word of its ties to gnolls, kobolds, and goblins. Gryan Stoutmantle needs this intelligence to measure the full reach of the conspiracy choking Westfall. Wiley the Black says telling what he knows about the Defias could cost him his life. Along the edges of Redridge and Westfall, he has caught wind of an operation far greater than highway robbery. His sealed note describes how the Brotherhood has coordinated groups that are usually hostile to one another across the countryside. Wiley warns that the Defias has drawn an alarming network around itself. The red-masked outlaws have enlisted gnoll packs, kobold diggers, and goblin engineers instead of working alone. Together, their brutal muscle, burrowing labor, and mechanical cunning point to an enterprise beyond what the People's Militia first expected. Gryan Stoutmantle has little love for Wiley and openly laments that he did not leave the rogue to rot when he had the chance. Yet Westfall cannot afford pride. With Stormwind ignoring pleas for military aid, the People's Militia must take useful intelligence wherever it can find it.

quest:1338.text: Stormpike's Order. In Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike is arranging a shield from Furen Longbeard. The armorsmith works far south in Stormwind City, so Stormpike asks a traveler to carry his order there. Mountaineer Stormpike wants a new shield, and he trusts only Furen Longbeard to forge it. The mountaineer is willing to pay well to place the commission in the smith’s hands, though Loch Modan and Stormwind City lie far apart. Stormpike wonders why Furen works so far from Ironforge and the Great Forge, where many dwarves make their home. He suspects Stormwind’s humans pay the smith a king’s ransom. When the order reaches Furen at his anvil, the armorsmith takes pride in hearing from the prestigious Stormpike clan and eagerly prepares to forge the shield.

quest:135.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's troubles reach Stormwind. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you to deliver Wiley's Note to Master Mathias Shaw, suspecting a link between the Defias and the old Stonemasons Guild. A mention of the Stonemasons in Wiley's communications catches Gryan Stoutmantle's attention. The builders rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War, but the guild has long been thought scattered or dissolved. If the Defias Brotherhood shares ties with them, Westfall's rural insurgency is more than a disorganized band of outlaws. From Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle cannot confirm his suspicions. He sends you to Master Mathias Shaw, head of Stormwind's covert intelligence wing, SI:7. Shaw works from the Barracks in Old Town, gathering whispers and secrets from across the realm. He may be able to untangle the Defias Brotherhood's origins.

quest:136.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A battered parchment map sets Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure in motion along Westfall's coast. The hunt begins with a search of the shoreline for the late captain's personal footlocker, then leads toward his hidden plunder across the region. Shipwrecks and the restless spirits of drowned sailors mark Westfall's western coast. Captain Sanders, an old seafarer, met a watery grave there. He left cryptic instructions so his hard-won fortune would not be lost to the Great Sea or taken by scavengers. A determined adventurer can retrace the trail he left behind.

quest:138.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. In Westfall, Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure sends you inland after a clue found by the shore. The trail leads east from the coast toward a barrel near ruined stonework. Captain Sanders sends you inland after the first cipher is solved. The clue points away from the shore and up the rocky bluffs, toward Westfall's main roads. An old chimney among roadside ruins marks the next stop. A discarded barrel nearby hides another message, and the ruined farmstead gives Sanders a landmark for the trail.

quest:139.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A broken barrel on Westfall's western shore holds Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure clue. It sends you north toward an old jug beside a coastal windmill, another step along the late pirate's trail to his hidden riches. Captain Sanders scattered his directions along Westfall's western shore. Each clue leads only to the next container, never straight to the prize. You have to follow the trail from one barrel, chest, or jug to another across the bluffs to reach his plunder. From the broken barrel, the parchment points due north toward the sea cliffs. Beside an isolated windmill on the bluffs, an abandoned jug holds the next clue. Murlocs and Defias scavengers roam coastal Westfall, so the way north carries danger.

quest:140.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A whiskey-soaked clue sends Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure hunt west from Westfall's shore. The trail leads out across the Great Sea, away from the mainland's troubles, to a remote islet. Captain Sanders scattered clues along Westfall's coast for any adventurer bold enough to follow them. The last parchment came from the dregs of his favorite whiskey jug and gives the final bearing. The captain's words are clear: head west to the water's edge, then swim out into the waves.

quest:141.text: The Defias Brotherhood. Mathias Shaw sends a confidential report from Stormwind to Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Shaw has investigated the former Stonemasons Guild to help Stoutmantle uncover the origins of the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:144.text: Messenger to Westfall. A letter from Westfall brings Magistrate Solomon a hard answer in Lakeshire. He asked Gryan Stoutmantle for soldiers to defend Redridge, but Westfall has been left to face its own troubles. Magistrate Solomon faces growing troubles in the Redridge Mountains without Stormwind's royal garrison. He looks to the southern frontier for help and writes to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia in Westfall. Solomon hopes the volunteers at Sentinel Hill can spare fighters to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. He does not know how hard pressed the western plains are. Gryan Stoutmantle refuses, though the answer weighs heavily on him. Westfall is fighting the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls because the House of Nobles and the crown have abandoned the kingdom's breadbasket. The People's Militia formed so the people could survive. Its ranks lose good men each day, and Stoutmantle cannot spare a single fighter for Redridge.

quest:147.text: Manhunt. Marshal Dughan sends you after a Defias bagman called the Collector in Elwynn Forest. The Collector works from the overrun Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and sends stolen gold from the forest's mines into the Brotherhood's coffers. Marshal Dughan sends you to Brackwell Pumpkin Patch after Elwynn's gnolls are found carrying a schedule for gold pickups. Defias bandits and gnolls have taken over the once quiet homestead. The Collector hides among its overgrown vines, skimming ore from the kingdom's mines and arranging shipments for the growing rebellion.

quest:15.text: Investigate Echo Ridge. Marshal McBride sends recruits north as kobolds gather at Echo Ridge Mine. The mine supplies ore and raw materials to Northshire Abbey and the Stormwind guard, and the growing threat puts both at risk. After early skirmishes with scattered vermin around Northshire's forested edge, scouts report a more organized threat. Kobolds have gathered in force at Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride sends you north to face the workers at the entrance and learn how deeply they have settled in. Echo Ridge Mine supplies ore and raw materials to the Northshire brotherhood and the Stormwind guard stationed there. Kobolds have seized the tunnels, halting extraction and exposing the strain on local defenses. McBride asks you to cull ten workers, but the infestation runs deeper into the shafts than a surface patrol can reach.

quest:151.text: Poor Old Blanchy. Verna Furlbrow waits beside the road in Westfall with her stranded family and starving mare. Their wagon broke during an attempt to escape, leaving Old Blanchy exhausted. Verna asks you to gather oats from nearby abandoned farmsteads and feed the old horse. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow are stranded beside Westfall's main road. Bandits and rogue mechanical harvest golems have driven families like theirs from their homes. As the Furlbrows tried to haul their belongings to safety, their wagon broke down, leaving them marooned in open country. Old Blanchy has plowed and hauled for the Furlbrow family across many seasons. Now exhausted from pulling their overloaded cart and starved by the delay, the gentle mare is fading fast. Verna asks you to search nearby overrun farmsteads for sacks of oats, where hostile threshers and gnoll scavengers threaten. The grain could give the faithful animal a decent meal.

quest:152.text: The Coast Isn't Clear. Along Westfall's western shore, shipwrecked sailors face murloc tribes on the beaches. Captain Grayson at the Westfall Lighthouse calls for help clearing the coast so survivors can reach land safely. Westfall's western coast has claimed countless ships. Reefs, sudden squalls, and jagged rocks break vessels against the shoals. Survivors may cling to wreckage and crawl ashore, hoping for rescue. But murloc tribes control the beaches and show no mercy to castaways. Captain Grayson tends the Westfall Lighthouse from a lonely outcropping southwest of the mainland. Death has bound him to the post, yet he remains watchful over passing ships and sailors in need. Murlocs make the shore deadly, from Coastrunners in the north to Tidehunters, Warriors, and Oracles in the south. Grayson calls on travelers to clear the coastline.

quest:153.text: Red Leather Bandanas. At Sentinel Hill, Red Leather Bandanas mark the fight against the Defias Brotherhood. Scout Galiaan offers a reward for the red cloth masks worn by the outlaws, as the People's Militia struggles to track them across Westfall. Across Westfall, the red bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. The gang draws cutpurses, looters, and traitors from many walks of life, but its members rally beneath the same crimson sign. Scout Galiaan and the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill collect the bandanas as proof that bandits have fallen. The cloth also helps them follow the Defias as their fronts shift across the countryside. Stormwind has denied Westfall proper military support, so the People's Militia depends on seasoned observers like Scout Galiaan to chart Defias activity. Galiaan watches outlaw patrols from Sentinel Hill. Passing adventurers and militia volunteers take on the dangerous work of bringing down the highwaymen who have driven honest farmers from their land.

quest:155.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the People's Militia seeks the Defias Brotherhood's hidden base. A turncoat agrees to guide Alliance champions there in exchange for protection. The road passes through Moonbrook, where Edwin VanCleef's inner sanctum lies hidden. Gryan Stoutmantle's fight against the Defias Brotherhood reaches a turning point when a captured brigand agrees to talk. His former brothers may execute or assassinate him, so the Defias Traitor bargains with the People's Militia. Escort him safely through hostile territory, and he will reveal where Edwin VanCleef and his ringleaders hide. The thieves' network silences those who speak out, and the turncoat needs armed protection along the road.

quest:1582.text: Moonglow Vest. Moonglow Vest is a trade training task offered by the night elf leatherworker Lotherias in Darnassus. Overwhelmed by the constant needs of young adventurers heading into the wilds of Kalimdor, she trades the knowledge of a specialized night elven tunic pattern in exchange for bulk shipments of embossed leather gear. In the sheltered boughs of Darnassus, tradesmen work tirelessly to outfit the swelling ranks of sentinels and aspiring wilderness scouts. As young night elves and allied wanderers venture forth beyond Teldrassil into a volatile Kalimdor, reliable armor is in fierce demand. Master leatherworkers like Lotherias bear the burden of keeping these frontiers supplied with sturdy hides. To ensure her apprentices possess both endurance and technical precision, Lotherias requires proof of their handiwork through multiple matched garments: embossed gloves, boots, and cloaks. Meeting this quota earns her trust, prompting her to impart the distinct night elven pattern for the Moonglow Vest—a garment favored for balancing supple protection with agile mobility.

quest:1598.text: The Stolen Tome. In Northshire Valley, a novice human warlock is sent to recover a forbidden tome and prove their skill. Drusilla La Salle hopes to claim Powers of the Void from the Defias, whose camp lies in the vineyards. Warlocks in Stormwind's lands hide their craft and keep prying eyes from their research. Northshire Abbey guards forbidden grimoires in its archives. Drusilla La Salle, the warlock mentor on the abbey grounds, covets Powers of the Void but cannot risk suspicion from the clerics and paladins by entering the library's protected wing herself. An abbey novice joins the Defias Brotherhood and steals several valuable texts on his way out. He flees to the Northshire Vineyards and takes refuge around the Defias campsite. The thieves stash their prize in a field tent, unaware of the danger in the book's dark arts. Recovering the tome tests a novice warlock's nerve and opens the way to darker knowledge. Braving the bandit camp and returning the text satisfies Drusilla's ambition and proves the pupil is ready. She rewards the pupil with the dark rites to summon and bind an imp, the first demon an apprentice learns to command.

quest:16.text: Give Gerard a Drink. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works long days in the fields and needs fresh spring water. He trades apples for water brought by passing travelers. Elwynn Forest's farms supply grain, fruit, and vegetables to Stormwind's townsfolk and garrisons. Tending crops under the open sky is hot, demanding work. Gerard Tiller spends long days in the dirt at the Maclure Vineyards, keeping pests away and managing the harvest. With little time to return to town wells, he relies on passing recruits to bring clean spring water so he can keep working. Gerard trades provisions instead of coin. Travelers with extra flasks of Refreshing Spring Water can exchange them for fresh apples from the orchard. The kingdom stretches its resources to maintain order and feed its army, so direct barter between smallholders and recruits remains a practical way to get by in rural Elwynn.

quest:1638.text: A Warrior's Training. In Goldshire, A Warrior's Training sends young warriors to Stormwind for lessons in battlefield endurance. Lyria Du Lac directs them to the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Old Town, where veteran Harry Burlguard offers seasoned instruction. After aspiring fighters show reliable command of the fundamentals against threats across Elwynn Forest, their trainers see little more for Goldshire drillmasters to teach. Lyria Du Lac sends recruits into Stormwind, toward the gritty district of Old Town. Veteran fighters gather there to share combat experience far from the royal garrison’s rigid ways. Harry Burlguard, an aged battle veteran, keeps his quarters at the Pig and Whistle Tavern. He tests a warrior’s mettle with tavern grit and practical stamina instead of parade-ground drills. Before teaching defensive maneuvers that help soldiers survive dangerous campaigns, Harry expects new arrivals to match his appetite for drink and face local brawlers in the tavern.

quest:1639.text: Bartleby the Drunk. In the Pig and Whistle Tavern, Bartleby the Drunk faces a test set by Harry Burlguard. An aspiring Alliance warrior must take Bartleby's prized mug before Harry will teach deeper combat skills. Harry Burlguard asks for proof of a novice's backbone before teaching deeper combat skills in the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Across the room, Bartleby nurses his drinks at the far end of the counter. Harry wants you to take the man's mug, knowing Bartleby would rather fight than surrender his ale. The challenge puts a warrior's resolve to the test. Soldiers, laborers, and rough locals fill the Pig and Whistle, where polished manners count for little. Bartleby mocks newcomers as too prissy for a tavern scuffle instead of answering politely. The exchange leads to a brawl on the floorboards, where a warrior's training in Stormwind begins with a test of basic barroom fighting.

quest:1640.text: Beat Bartleby. In Stormwind, Bartleby guards the mug a young warrior must claim. The instructors send recruits to face him in a bare-knuckle fight and earn the vessel for their training. Stormwind's warrior instructors expect recruits to face combat without excuses or grand ceremony. As part of their formal training, young warriors must retrieve a particular mug from Bartleby, a notorious drunkard who lounges in the city. He scoffs at polite requests and swears no one will take his prized drinkware without prying it from his cold, dead fingers. For a fledgling warrior, words soon give way to a fistfight. Bartleby boasts that he will fight to the death, but a thorough thrashing is enough to sober him. Once beaten, his bravado gives way to bruised admiration. He recognizes that his opponent is tougher than they appear and yields peacefully, letting the victor claim the mug and complete the trial at the training hall.

quest:1641.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, The Tome of Divinity guides young paladins through a solemn rite. Under Duthorian Rall's care in the Cathedral of Light, you face teachings on virtue, devotion, and the duties that come with the Holy Light. Duthorian Rall guides those who answer the paladin's calling in the Cathedral of Light. Early training teaches martial discipline and the order's rites, but advancement asks for a deeper commitment to the spirit. The trials ask you to look beyond battle and weigh the moral duties of a paladin. Stormwind faces dangers within its borders and beyond, and its people need defenders who understand that duty. Receiving the Book of Divinity binds you to service and self-sacrifice. Duthorian asks you to study the holy text and learn what the Light demands of its defenders. Its lessons prepare paladins to oppose the Scourge's creeping horrors and protect common folk. Righteous power must answer to virtue and compassion.

quest:1665.text: Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, Bartleby's Mug marks a young warrior's trial of grit. After besting Bartleby in the Pig and Whistle Tavern, you claim his drinking mug for your trainer, Harry Burlguard. Harry Burlguard tests young warriors with a brawl in Old Town. He asks you to take down Bartleby, a stubborn drunk at the bar of the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Once subdued, Bartleby reluctantly gives up his prized drinking mug, but first takes one final swig to drain the dregs. Returning the mug to Harry Burlguard completes your novice trial. Burlguard sees that you can persuade through sheer force and recognizes your readiness for defensive mastery. He points you onward to further battlefield instruction with Marshal Haggard, a seasoned veteran in Elwynn Forest.

quest:1666.text: Marshal Haggard. At Eastvale, Marshal Haggard keeps the arms he gathered over a lifetime of service. Harry Burlguard sends novice warriors from Stormwind City to meet the retired marshal and seek better weapons. Stormwind's novice warriors need more than skill to face danger beyond the city. Harry Burlguard sends promising fighters east through Elwynn Forest to find Marshal Haggard, a retired officer who served the realm for years. Haggard gathered a personal armory over a lifetime in the field, and his home near the Eastvale Logging Camp holds weapons for young warriors seeking better arms. Marshal Haggard lives in a secluded manor near the Eastvale Logging Camp. Years of service have weakened his failing sight, and he sometimes mistakes approaching travelers for prowling riverpaw gnolls. Though age keeps him in this quiet corner of eastern Elwynn, Stormwind's guards and trainers still respect the old marshal.

quest:1667.text: Dead-tooth Jack. A stolen badge puts Marshal Haggard's authority in Defias hands. The retired officer lives in eastern Elwynn Forest, where Dead-tooth Jack tricked him into surrendering his official insignia. Jack wore a Stormwind tabard in the dark and posed as Marshal Dughan. Haggard needs the badge back before the Defias Brotherhood can use it to impersonate Stormwind officials. Marshal Haggard lives in an isolated cottage on Elwynn's eastern ridges. One night, a figure in a Stormwind tabard approached, claiming official business and asking for Haggard's old marshal's badge. Believing he was handing it to a fellow officer, Haggard complied. The stranger laughed in his face and vanished into the woods. The thief was a Defias rogue called Dead-tooth Jack. Marshal Haggard has retired, but his old badge still carries the legal weight of Stormwind. Defias bandits are creeping across Elwynn, Westfall, and Redridge, and the badge could help them pass guard checkpoints, redirect patrols, or take command of supplies. Jack retreated to a camp to the south and left the badge locked in a strongbox. Haggard needs it recovered before the Defias can cause serious harm.

quest:1688.text: Surena Caledon. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin seeks his former pupil and a bloodstone choker. He sends an aspiring warlock after Surena Caledon, who betrayed him to join the Defias Brotherhood. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novices the forbidden arts of fel summoning. He once took a young woman named Surena Caledon as his pupil. He admired her natural magical talent and her beauty. Surena left her studies and Gakin's favor, then fled Stormwind with her lover, Erlan Drudgemoor, to join the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:1689.text: The Binding. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder puts a novice warlock through a final trial. With his recovered Bloodstone Choker, you draw a voidwalker into a hidden circle and force it to submit. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, forgotten catacombs run beyond the watchful gaze of the Silver Hand and Kirin Tor magistrates. Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novice warlocks that dark magic demands more than channeling power; they must also dominate otherworldly beings. You have recovered Gakin's stolen Bloodstone Choker from Surena Caledon. Now he asks you to call a voidwalker into the summoning circle beneath the tavern. A voidwalker will not bargain with you. The power in the Bloodstone Choker opens a rift and draws the shadow creature into the mortal world. You must batter it with magic and force until its will breaks, proving you can command it. Once defeated, the voidwalker's essence binds to you, giving you a durable, shadowy protector that can endure punishment in the battles ahead.

quest:18.text: Brotherhood of Thieves. Deputy Willem sends recruits across Northshire's eastern river to face the Defias Brotherhood. Their red burlap bandanas give Stormwind its first tangible evidence of the brigands' organized presence in the valley. Northshire Valley has long been a safe haven in Elwynn Forest, guarded by Stormwind and used to train recruits and Clerics of the Holy Light. Recently, discipline along its perimeter has frayed. Vagrants and thieves have crossed the eastern river, lurking near the woods and making small camps close to the abbey. Deputy Willem maintains local order, but the guards cannot spare the manpower to watch every corner of the valley without volunteers. These outlaws are coordinated and wear matching attire. They call themselves the Defias Brotherhood, and their red burlap bandanas mark their allegiance. Deputy Willem sends recruits to drive back the brigands and recover their masks, hoping to curb their advance and learn how deeply the Defias have reached into the kingdom's heartland.

quest:184.text: Furlbrow's Deed. The Furlbrows flee their farm as Defias bandits carry their land grant through Elwynn Forest. Returning the deed to Farmer Furlbrow near the Westfall border preserves the couple’s claim to their stolen homestead. Defias bandits in Elwynn carry a land deed signed by Theodore and Verna Furlbrow. A crude note on its back says they drove the elderly farmer from his property, then carried the document across the river into Elwynn to copy it and forge claims to other seized land. The note says the Furlbrows were stranded just over the border, beside the road, after their wagon broke. The Defias have driven dozens of families from their ancestral land in Westfall. With Stormwind’s army absent and the realm’s resources strained, the Brotherhood uses force and false claims to seize the kingdom’s breadbasket. Theodore and Verna are leaving their farm for safety, but their lawful deed preserves their claim if order ever returns to the province.

quest:1860.text: Speak with Jennea. In Goldshire, Zaldimar Wefhellt sends novice mages to Stormwind for further instruction. He directs apprentices who have advanced beyond basic training in Elwynn Forest to Jennea Cannon in the Wizard's Sanctum. Zaldimar Wefhellt sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind City as your training advances. Your time learning elementary spells from local tutors in Elwynn's hamlets has run its course. In the Mage Quarter, the Wizard's Sanctum is where the kingdom's senior mages pursue arcane study and instruction. They coordinate magical matters across the realm. Zaldimar says your report concerns the security of Elwynn Forest and Stormwind, not only your studies. In Stormwind, you report to Jennea Cannon, a mage who oversees local assignments. She is cautious about sharing grand secrets with a newly arrived apprentice, but your report begins your service to the wizarding order.

quest:1861.text: Mirror Lake. Novice Alliance mages in Stormwind's Mage Quarter are sent to sample Mirror Lake's waters for magical contamination. Jennea Cannon sends them southwest of the city gates to test the waterfall spray. Azeroth's arcane currents were shaken by conflicts from the opening of the Dark Portal through the Third War and the battle at Mount Hyjal. Those shocks tore ancient currents from their stable channels. In Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum, magi like Jennea Cannon watch the changes closely. They fear that displaced arcane power could reach the wilderness and corrupt local ecosystems. Mirror Lake lies beneath the cliffs southwest of the Stormwind gates and is a primary natural reservoir fed by mountain falls. The surrounding countryside depends on its waters. Jennea sends novice mages with a glass flask to the waterfall's base, where they collect fresh spray. The Sanctum can then use scrying and reagent tests to learn whether wild magic is seeping into the public water supply.

quest:1941.text: Manaweave Robe. In Stormwind, Wynne Larson presents the Manaweave Robe as a proud showcase for her family’s shop. She has woven the enchanted garment from fine materials for a commission that is now complete. Larson Clothiers serves spellcasters in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter with garments made to channel volatile energies. Fine magical robes call for rare materials, careful needlework, and threadwork that holds through mystic resonance. Wynne Larson takes pride in each piece that leaves her shop, where every robe worn into the field carries the Larson name. The manaweave robe offers comfort, mobility, and practical resilience for travel through contested lands. Once the needed components are delivered, Wynne Larson weaves the final stitch herself and presents the finished garment as a fine example of Larson tailoring, meant to draw admiration and spread the shop’s name across the kingdom.

quest:21.text: Skirmish at Echo Ridge. In Northshire Valley, recruits strike at kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride ordered the attack after scouts found the mine overrun. Marshal McBride sends recruits against the kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Scouts found the mine overrun, and the garrison fears the creatures will strengthen their hold if left alone. The kobolds dig through the tunnels, gather stolen resources, and multiply. Recruits must thin their numbers to protect Northshire Valley, with its farms and spiritual retreat. New recruits are sent into the mine because the Stormwind Army is stretched thin. Garrison forces guard the southern borders, while unrest is rumored across Elwynn. Officers like McBride must call on willing hands. A recruit who proves reliable at Echo Ridge earns the army’s respect and is ready for more difficult work elsewhere in the kingdom.

quest:22.text: Goretusk Liver Pie. At the Saldean Farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean prepares a pie amid hard times. Bandits have ravaged the breadbasket of the kingdom, and local homesteaders hunt aggressive boars to feed their families. Westfall was once Stormwind's fertile breadbasket, but hard times have fallen on the land. Neglected roads, roving outlaws, and overgrown fields make daily life a struggle for the few settlers who remain. At the Saldean Farm, Salma Saldean works to keep a sense of home despite the dangers around her. A traditional meat pie offers one of the few modest comforts for homesteaders trying to preserve their way of life. Goretusks roam Westfall's plains in great numbers, their tough hides and vicious tusks making them dangerous. They threaten lone farmhands, yet provide vital meat to families cut off from regular trade. Salma's recipe calls for crushed rosemary, minced garlic, chopped dill, and simmering gravy. With careful preparation, the pungent organs of these hardy beasts become a rich, savory meal.

quest:2205.text: Seek out SI: 7. In Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends new rogues toward SI: 7. A sealed package carried to Stormwind City brings them before Master Mathias Shaw, who leads the crown's covert intelligence network. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, rogue trainer Keryn Sylvius wastes no time praising newcomers. She thinks fresh initiates look more like cheese delivery hands than covert agents, yet gives them a sealed delivery for the capital. The trip tests their reliability as couriers and quietly vets scouts for wider service to the realm. SI: 7 works from the southeastern corner of Old Town in Stormwind City. The worn district holds the command center of Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7, where Master Mathias Shaw oversees the kingdom's covert operations. Shaw receives the package with dry skepticism and judges whether the traveler has the grit for real espionage.

quest:2206.text: Snatch and Grab. Master Mathias Shaw sends agents to Jerod's Landing for shipping intelligence. The Defias Brotherhood uses the river dock to move supplies in secret. Master Mathias Shaw tests aspiring operatives who seek a place in Stormwind's covert intelligence wing. He asks for finesse and stealth, not brute force. SI:7 agents take down key figures quietly and recover important papers without drawing the realm into open scandal. Each new operative must prove they can work unseen. Jerod's Landing lies on the river in southern Elwynn, south of Goldshire and just east of the Maclure Vineyards. The Defias Brotherhood seized the once-quiet dock and made it an illicit route. Smuggled arms, supplies, and contraband cross the water from Redridge toward Westfall, beyond the reach of royal road patrols. Master Mathias Shaw warns agents that capture, compromise, or death leaves them without the Crown's support. Stormwind and its spymasters will deny knowing they ever existed. Recovering the Defias Dockmaster's schedule gives SI:7 proof of the Brotherhood's supply lines while keeping Stormwind's official involvement hidden.

quest:2281.text: Redridge Rendezvous. Promising Alliance rogues are sent east from Stormwind’s intelligence headquarters to train in Lakeshire. SI:7 wants them ready for dangerous field work under seasoned operatives. Renzik 'The Shiv', SI:7’s second-in-command in Stormwind, warns that untrained rogues rarely survive dangerous operations. Sending raw recruits into hostile territory brings casualties instead of intelligence. SI:7 sends promising agents east to the Redridge Mountains, where they train under Lucius, stationed among Lakeshire’s docks. Lakeshire offers an ideal ground for clandestine training. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs threaten the frontier town, while its piers give Lucius cover to test a rogue’s stealth, reflexes, and lockpicking without attracting townspeople or guards.

quest:2300.text: SI:7. In Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends promising young rogues toward Stormwind's hidden ranks. Recruits report to Renzik "The Shiv" in Old Town, where they enter Master Mathias Shaw's service. Keryn Sylvius watches local recruits from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. When a rogue proves cunning and capable against the growing Defias threat, Sylvius passes along a message from headquarters. The order is plain: report to Renzik "The Shiv" without delay. The recruit leaves Elwynn's fields for the covert heart of Stormwind. Behind an unassuming barracks in Old Town, SI:7 keeps its headquarters. Master Mathias Shaw commands the agency, whose work includes covert operations, reconnaissance, and assassination across the kingdom and beyond. Renzik "The Shiv," Shaw's sharp-tongued second-in-command, assesses promising agents before sending them into dangerous work beyond the reach of the kingdom's formal military.

quest:239.text: Westbrook Garrison Needs Help!. Marshal Dughan sends available adventurers west to Westbrook Garrison, the outpost at Elwynn Forest's border with Westfall. Stormwind's army is stretched thin across the kingdom, while Deputy Rainer and his guards face growing pressure from Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves without regular reinforcements. Westbrook Garrison guards the western edge of Elwynn Forest, where settled woodland meets Westfall's troubled plains. Gnoll warbands and bandits grow bolder along the waterways and western roads, and the small garrison has asked for more men. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's administration have no Stormwind soldiers to spare. Local commanders must hire traveling mercenaries and wandering adventurers. Deputy Rainer and his men face the Riverpaw gnolls, whose raiding parties harass travelers and nearby homesteads. The pack operates in the borderlands between Elwynn and Westfall. With Stormwind distracted by political and military troubles, the gnolls press deeper into inhabited territory. Westbrook Garrison guards against their unchecked advance into the heart of the forest.

quest:2998.text: Tome of Divinity. A summons bearing the Tome of Divinity calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Answering Brother Wilhelm's call begins the sacred trials needed to master resurrection through the Holy Light. Novice paladins in Elwynn Forest spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows martial discipline and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. Leaders of the paladins take note of promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind and report straight to the kingdom's spiritual heart. In Cathedral Square, Stormwind's Cathedral of Light is the supreme sanctuary of the kingdom's priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Duthorian Rall resides there and oversees those sworn to the Order. Beneath its soaring vaulted ceilings, high-ranking paladins set formal trials from the Tome of Divinity before each initiate. The challenges test compassion, fortitude, and a willingness to sacrifice.

quest:3104.text: Glyphic Letter. A sealed summons reaches novice human mages in Northshire Valley, sent by Marshal McBride. Khelden Bremen calls promising spellcasters to Northshire Abbey to begin their arcane tutelage. Marshal McBride gives the rune-marked letter to an aspiring apprentice who has proved capable by helping him against local vermin. Khelden Bremen, Northshire's resident mage trainer, wrote it. He watches new recruits arriving at the abbey for signs of magical discipline and talent. Northshire Abbey has long been a sanctuary of the Holy Light, but Stormwind's dangers call for practitioners of every discipline. The letter brings you upstairs to Khelden Bremen. He offers no easy praise. Instead, he warns that mastering arcane power means defying natural limits, earning both profound respect and deep fear from ordinary folk.

quest:3105.text: Tainted Letter. At Northshire, Tainted Letter calls novice human warlocks away from the Abbey guards for instruction in the fel arts. Drusilla La Salle entrusts it to Marshal McBride, who delivers it to her recruits. Novice warlocks receive a letter from Marshal McBride after proving themselves against the kobold menace. While priests and paladins study openly in Northshire Abbey, warlocks must tread carefully. Drusilla La Salle's insignia marks the letter, which directs each fledgling spellcaster to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before taking on other duties. Drusilla warns that warlocks walk a precarious path under the watchful eyes of Stormwind's guards, whom she calls 'pathetic mundanes.' Drawing power from the Twisting Nether and communing with demons always risk corruption. She counsels patience, prudence, and firm self-control when handling those dark energies, but says caution must not extinguish a warlock's ambition.

quest:33.text: Wolves Across the Border. Eagan Peltskinner asks you to hunt wolves prowling Northshire Valley and bring him their meat. He waits outside Northshire Abbey, where the valley’s needs continue despite the guards’ focus on Defias bandits. Eagan Peltskinner waits by Northshire Abbey’s walls with a grudge against the local timber wolves. Marshal McBride and the Stormwind guards have limited strength to defend the abbey from Defias bandits, while tradesfolk still have daily needs. Eagan asks you to thin the wolves’ numbers and bring back their tough meat for his cooking. Wolves roam closer to Northshire Abbey as patrols weaken. The Kingdom of Stormwind has too few troops and is strained by missing leadership. Young wolves and timber wolves now prowl the abbey’s paths and orchards. Hunting them supplies Eagan’s pantry and makes nearby trails safer for novitiates, laborers, and newly arrived defenders.

quest:332.text: Wine Shop Advert. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina draws passersby to his family's wine shop. He offers a voucher for a free bottle of vintage wine from their canal-side storefront, a small sign of trade in the reconstructed capital. Everyday life in Stormwind revolves around brisk commerce. Renato Gallina walks the Trade District's cobbled streets, promoting Gallina Winery, the small shop he runs with his sister, Suzetta. He hands flyers to thirsty travelers and locals, each offering a free tasting. The Gallina family offers a bottle of their famous pinot noir. Follow the ticket to the winery entrance near the canals, where Suzetta Gallina hands over the bottle. The family hopes a taste of their signature wine will bring newcomers back.

quest:333.text: Harlan Needs a Resupply. Harlan Bagley, a Stormwind merchant, cannot keep sturdy clothes and armor in stock. As demand surges, he sends an urgent cloth order to Rema Schneider at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, unaware of the conflicts brewing beyond the city walls. Across Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley's shelves are emptying fast. Citizens and wandering adventurers are buying reinforced tunics, traveling clothes, and battle-ready armor. Harlan wonders if people are preparing for a harsh season or winter, but the rush has left his shop short of finished cloth. Harlan sends a runner across the city's waterways to Rema Schneider, a seamstress at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is glad of his trade, yet the sudden demand for protective clothing troubles her. Rumors of tension spread through the kingdom, and Rema wonders whether the House of Nobles is hiding talk of open war from ordinary people.

quest:334.text: Package for Thurman. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider needs her son Thurman’s tailoring supplies at Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. He left home without his shears and needles, and Rema asks you to carry them to his workshop. Rema Schneider worries that Thurman will fall behind in his tailoring work without his shears and needles. He left home in a rush, and his mother asks you to carry the tools across Stormwind’s canals to his workshop.

quest:35.text: Further Concerns. Marshal Dughan sends an Alliance courier east from Goldshire to check reports of danger. You cross Elwynn Forest to speak with Guard Thomas, who watches the river crossing toward Redridge. Rumors tell of hostile aquatic creatures creeping along Elwynn's riverbanks. Marshal Dughan commands the Goldshire garrison, where banditry and vermin already trouble the center of the forest. He will not dismiss the reports, but he cannot spare guards from town. Instead, he sends you east to consult Guard Thomas, the sentry at the bridge over the river toward Redridge. Guard Thomas has held the bridge outpost for more than a week and has seen what Goldshire's leaders only feared. Hostile, semi-intelligent murlocs have made camps along the waterways of eastern Elwynn. Stormwind's army is absent, while local garrisons protect town walls and supply lines. That leaves rural bridge posts like Thomas's isolated before the growing danger.

quest:353.text: Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The road leads from Stormwind's Dwarven District to an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make a weapon for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The Stormpike clan is respected in Ironforge for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore turns to trustworthy travelers to carry the axe north, across the distance between Stormwind and the dwarven borderlands. At Loch Modan's northern guard tower, Mountaineer Stormpike watches over lands troubled by wandering troggs and burrowing kobolds. The southern human kingdoms face rumors of unrest and banditry, while the dwarven frontier has dangers of its own. Stormpike needs a new blade to help keep the mountain passes secure.

quest:36.text: Westfall Stew. In Westfall, another family is leaving its farm as banditry drives homesteaders from their land. Before departing, Verna Furlbrow entrusts her cherished local recipe to Salma Saldean. Defias thieves and wild mechanical harvest reapers have driven Verna and Farmer Furlbrow from their family acreage. They pack their wagon and prepare to seek refuge behind Stormwind's walls. Before leaving, Verna gives her neighbor Salma Saldean the recipe for Westfall Stew, hoping the farm's home-cooked tradition will live on. Salma Saldean and her husband, Farmer Saldean, still hold their homestead just down the road. Verna's recipe marks the loss of another neighbor to the unrest, yet keeps a local farm tradition alive. Salma sets out to gather the ingredients needed to feed those still struggling on the frontier.

quest:37.text: Find the Lost Guards. Guard Thomas is waiting at Elwynn's eastern bridge for word of two missing guards. Rolf and Malakai were sent north along the river to watch for murlocs, but neither has returned. Guard Thomas watches the eastern crossing of Elwynn Forest, where the King's road approaches Redridge. Murlocs have made the nearby waters more dangerous. Days ago, Thomas sent two Stormwind guards, Rolf and Malakai, north along the riverbanks to scout the threat and clear out nests. Neither has returned, and Thomas fears violence stopped their patrol.

quest:38.text: Westfall Stew. Salma Saldean cooks Westfall Stew on her farm, making a meal from what the frontier offers. Its ingredients reflect how Westfall homesteaders endure bandits, famine, and dangerous beasts. Westfall's settlers contend with bandits, famine, and rampaging beasts, far from Stormwind's lavish larders. Families like the Saldeans make do with what the land provides. Salma Saldean turns ingredients many city folk might call pests or scraps into a sustaining meal for working farmhands. Salma's recipe brings together local okra, stringy meat from circling vultures, and snouts from wild goretusks roaming the plains. It also calls for fresh murloc eyes gathered from coastal raiders. The thought of river beasts and carrion birds may turn delicate stomachs in Elwynn, but Westfall cooks swear the blend makes a rich, fortifying meal.

quest:3861.text: CLUCK!. In Westfall, a chicken may answer when you call and feed it. Follow its scratched message to the Saldean family, and a warm egg may be yours to hatch. Ordinary chickens wander the farmsteads of Azeroth, and most travelers pass them by. Mimic a chicken's gestures and clucking, and it may stop pecking to regard you with interest. In that brief moment, the bird scratches letters in the dirt. The message points to the farmer who can provide the food it wants. The bird's request calls for Special Chicken Feed. In Westfall, the Saldean family keeps this grain for their flock. Offer the feed and cheer the chicken on as it eats. In return, it lays a warm egg that can be nurtured into a feathered companion.

quest:39.text: Deliver Thomas' Report. In eastern Elwynn, Guard Thomas sends word of two dead guards and rising danger. He asks you to carry the report to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, where the garrison has few hands to spare. Guard Thomas watches the bridges into eastern Elwynn, where river traffic meets the wilderness. Guards Malakai and Rolf have been killed by aggressive murloc tribes. With his remaining guards too few to contain them, Thomas sends you down the road to Goldshire with an urgent report. Marshal Dughan receives Thomas' report in Goldshire, already struggling to keep patrols on the roads. Kobolds infest the area, Defias bandits threaten travelers, and Stormwind City has sent no reinforcements. The deaths of two experienced guards add to his burden. Murlocs may soon threaten Goldshire itself, while the defenses across the region grow ever thinner.

quest:3903.text: Milly Osworth. At Northshire Abbey, Deputy Willem sends you to help Milly Osworth. Her wagon and livelihood are in jeopardy, and she needs help across the abbey grounds. The work takes you from defending the abbey to aiding Elwynn Forest's civilians. After you prove your mettle against the Defias thieves encroaching on Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem recognizes you as capable and willing to help. He sends you to assist his friend Milly Osworth. This favor is personal, outside the abbey's official guard duties, and Milly is a civilian caught in the valley's growing unrest. Milly waits beside her wagon on the far side of Northshire Abbey, near the stables. Deputy Willem must stay at his post to defend the abbey. Milly's troubles lie out in the valley, where the stretched guard garrison has too few hands to help her.

quest:3904.text: Milly's Harvest. Defias brigands have driven Milly Osworth from the Northshire vineyards. Her harvest lies scattered in buckets and crates among the occupied rows, where it may be stolen or crushed. Milly Osworth fled the southeastern fields of Northshire Valley when Defias brigands swarmed the vines. She left her gathered grapes behind in buckets and crates among the occupied rows. Northshire's garrison is stretched thin, and Milly fears that boots and fighting will crush any fruit the bandits leave behind. Defias bandits now occupy working vineyards, a sign of how little safety Northshire can offer. Stormwind's attention is elsewhere, and the valley has too few guards. Farmers like Milly must depend on recruits and wanderers to protect their property and secure the food and wine that supply the abbey.

quest:3905.text: Grape Manifest. Milly Osworth records her rescued grape harvest for Northshire Abbey. She writes a manifest of the yield recovered from Defias thieves, then sends it to Brother Neals so the brotherhood can replenish its wine stores. Northshire Valley's soil and orchards have long supported local food and the abbey's wine. When thieves and bandits seized the eastern fields, they cut off the abbey's supply of grapes and food. With the harvest recovered from the occupied fields, Milly Osworth records the yield in a manifest. Brother Neals oversees food and drink at Northshire Abbey. He is known for sampling Northshire's vintages in the quiet of the bell tower. Brigands still threaten the gates, but fresh grapes give the brotherhood a moment to toast the Light and take heart.

quest:399.text: Humble Beginnings. Baros Alexston seeks help from his home in Stormwind's Cathedral Square. His family's Westfall farm has burned, and thieves hold its ruins; he hopes to recover an heirloom from his youth. Baros Alexston grew up working the fields of Westfall. Now he is an accomplished architect in Stormwind City, advising on stonework and city buildings. His path from farm boy to city planner is rare in the kingdom, yet he remains attached to the modest beginnings that shaped him. Lawlessness swept across Westfall, and the Alexston Farmstead fell to it. Bandits and vagrants burned the house, forcing Baros's father from his livelihood. Family heirlooms were left behind amid the fire and occupation. Baros asks you to search the ruined, bandit-held farmstead west of Sentinel Hill for his first compass, hidden before the home fell.

quest:40.text: A Fishy Peril. In Goldshire, A Fishy Peril begins with reports of murlocs moving inland through the waterways. Remy "Two Times" asks travelers to alert Marshal Dughan, whose guards are already stretched thin. Remy "Two Times" grows uneasy over a new threat while seeking business in Goldshire. Murlocs are creeping up the streams and into inland shallows, disrupting fishing and menacing innocent travelers. Remy fears the local guard is overlooking a danger that is still growing, so he asks passersby to carry word to the heart of the township. Marshal Dughan hears the report in Goldshire but remains skeptical. He is charged with protecting the realm while royal forces are stretched thin elsewhere, and Riverpaw gnolls and Defias highwaymen already demand his attention. With no confirmed military intelligence, he will not divert his scarce men to pursue rumors of fish-men in the eastern streams.

quest:45.text: Discover Rolf's Fate. In eastern Elwynn, two Stormwind guards are missing near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains and webbed tracks lead toward a murloc village, where the search for Rolf continues. Guard Thomas sent patrols around eastern Elwynn Forest as threats grew, but Malakai and Rolf vanished near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains lie by the shore. Webbed footprints pressed into the mud lead east along the water's edge, straight to a ramshackle murloc camp.

quest:4513.text: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. Following his initial study of tainted specimens, the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle seeks untainted ooze samples to understand how these strange creatures adapt to their environment. Having realized that oozes absorb the corrupted nature of places like Felwood, he sends adventurers to discover and gather pure, unpolluted specimens from across Kalimdor. Laris Geardawdle's preliminary experiments in Ironforge hit an immediate stumbling block: the oozes he previously examined were thoroughly polluted by the dark energies of Felwood. While this demonstrated that oozes absorb and reflect the traits of their surroundings, it left him without a control group. To understand the baseline nature of ooze life, he needs specimens untouched by demonic taint or urban filth.

quest:46.text: Bounty on Murlocs. Murlocs are spreading through eastern Elwynn, and the Stormwind Army has put a bounty on them. With the garrison stretched thin, Guard Thomas turns to travelers to clear the shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and the southern waterways before the murlocs overrun nearby farms and roads. Murlocs have made shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and along the fork of the southern streams. Lurkers and foragers now attack travelers and press toward human settlements. What began as a minor nuisance has grown into a threat across eastern Elwynn, while the western roads remain comparatively secure. Guard Thomas is stationed at the eastern bridge beside the Redridge Mountains, where dangers beyond the bridge and disorder at home compete for his attention. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and Stormwind's military command is mired in bureaucracy. Town garrisons rarely get the reinforcements they request. Marshal Dughan and local officers have turned to public bounties, offering coin for murloc fins to slow the attacks along the waterways.

quest:47.text: Gold Dust Exchange. At Goldshire's crossroads, Gold Dust Exchange brings Remy "Two Times" coin for gold dust from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. Travelers gather the dust and trade it to the nervous broker for pay. Goldshire sits where Elwynn Forest's roads meet, and travelers, merchants, and guards pass through town. Remy "Two Times" is a shady broker with a habit of repeating his words and a sharp eye for profit. Instead of paying mining crews to dig for raw minerals, he turns to travelers passing through the Lion's Pride Inn. He offers coin for gold dust taken from the kobolds in the region. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. These rat-like tunnelers chip through the dark for candles and shiny baubles, gathering flecks of unrefined ore in their pouches. Pushing them back serves the kingdom, and gathering their dust turns the work into a trade for coin.

quest:52.text: Protect the Frontier. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern bridge as predators threaten the frontier. Stormwind's forces are thin here, and wolves and bears have grown bold near the Eastvale Logging Camp. He asks capable adventurers to cull the beasts threatening travelers and workers. Guard Thomas watches the bridge over the river at Elwynn Forest's eastern edge. Goldshire and the Northshire Valley have a visible Stormwind garrison, but this frontier receives far less protection. With Stormwind's forces stretched across the realm, Thomas is one of few sentries between the settled heartlands and the wilderness. Travelers help keep vital supply roads open. Eastvale Logging Camp supplies timber to Stormwind City, but woodsmen felling trees at the forest's edge meet dangerous wildlife. Prowlers, gray forest wolves, and young forest bears now roam near roads and lumber yards. Culling them eases the danger to local workers for a time. Thomas suspects a disturbance deeper in the woods is driving the beasts toward settlements.

quest:5261.text: Eagan Peltskinner. Outside Northshire Abbey, Eagan Peltskinner has work for recruits as timber wolves threaten the valley. The local furrier needs hunters to thin the packs and bring back pelts. Deputy Willem often sends recruits from the abbey to find Eagan Peltskinner, who works nearby on its grounds. Northshire Valley's orchards and fields lie beside wild woods where timber wolves prowl. Eagan wants newcomers to hunt the aggressive packs and gather pelts for his craft. Timber wolves threaten workers, acolytes, and supplies moving in and out of Northshire. Sending young champions to Eagan helps keep nearby paths safe while sparing Stormwind's few remaining guards. They are already occupied by rising tensions across Elwynn Forest.

quest:543.text: The Perenolde Tiara. Count Remington Ridgewell seeks a lost heirloom in the Ruins of Alterac. The Stormwind aristocrat sends mercenaries north to recover the Perenolde Tiara, once owned by Alterac's royal family and now said to be held by an ogre mage. Alterac's royal family wore an emerald-set tiara crafted by master dwarven jewelers in Ironforge. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Grand Alliance and joined the Orcish Horde. His betrayal led to Alterac's conquest and collapse. In the fall of Alterac City, many treasures of the royal family vanished among the snowy rubble of the Alterac Mountains. Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage of the Crushridge ogres, came to hold the tiara among the ruins of Alterac. He searches the broken stones for baubles and abandoned wealth. Count Remington Ridgewell, a collector of historical oddities in Stormwind City, learns the tiara survived. He hires mercenaries to enter ogre-held territory, defeat Grel'borg, and bring the jewel back to his gallery.

quest:5502.text: A Warden of the Horde. A Warden of the Horde concludes Children's Week by returning Grunth to Orphan Matron Battlewail in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. After seeing the world with his guardian, the young orphan hopes to become a hero himself. After the adventures of Children's Week, Grunth thanks his guardian for showing him more than he ever dreamed he would see. Remembering his parents' advice to rise above hardship, he says he hopes to become a hero like the adventurer. His final request is to return home and tell the matron about their time together. Returning to the orphanage in the Valley of Honor, adventurers return their young charge back into the care of Orphan Matron Battlewail. Taking responsibility for the young is considered a profound duty in the new Horde, where war has left countless children without parents. Battlewail commends your compassion as the true measure of a hero of the Horde, and Grunth parts ways with a beloved pet to ensure you remember the bond forged during your travels.

quest:5545.text: A Bundle of Trouble. At Eastvale Logging Camp, A Bundle of Trouble begins with timber left in the woods and a deadline near. Supervisor Raelen needs the cut wood brought back before the shipment falls behind. Supervisor Raelen has a shipment of timber due soon. Eastvale Logging Camp cuts wood for Stormwind, and her crew has fallen behind schedule. With the deadline close, Raelen needs the timber sent on its way. Wolves and bears north of the camp have driven the woodcutters away from bundles of cut timber. The workers left the wood where it lay. Raelen cannot wait for guards to clear the area, so she asks you to bring the bundles back to camp.

quest:5623.text: In Favor of the Light. Priestess Anetta sends you south from Northshire Abbey to continue your training in Goldshire. Priestess Josetta is waiting at the Lion's Pride Inn to guide your next steps in the Holy Light. Northshire Abbey gives you shelter and your first lessons in the Holy Light. After you learn prayer and divine healing, Priestess Anetta sends you south along the road to Goldshire. There, you leave the abbey's sheltered study for service among the people of Elwynn. Priestess Josetta tends to Goldshire's spiritual needs from the Lion's Pride Inn and guides rising acolytes. She builds on the lessons you learned at the abbey, teaching you to offer comfort, protect the faithful, and heal the injured. Under her guidance, you begin learning the duties of the Church's servants across the kingdom.

quest:5624.text: Garments of the Light. At Goldshire, Garments of the Light mark a novice priest’s first trial under Priestess Josetta. She sends you east to Crystal Lake to tend the wounded Guard Roberts. The work tests your healing and earns you vestments recognized by the Church of the Holy Light. Priestess Josetta teaches acolytes who come to Goldshire from Northshire Abbey. Before the Church of the Holy Light formally recognizes a novice, she tests their skill with divine power. When Guard Roberts is reported wounded by the lake east of Goldshire, Josetta sends you to care for him. His need gives you a chance to prove your healing in practice. You need to do more than close Guard Roberts’s wounds. Mend him with restorative prayers, then strengthen him with a blessing of fortitude. Stormwind’s forces are stretched thin, and local garrisons face kobolds and bandits. Josetta teaches that priests help defenders endure danger. Healing Roberts will aid the township and show that you can support its guards. After treating Guard Roberts, return to the Lion’s Pride Inn. There you receive your first formal robes, a sign of approval and fellowship from the priesthood in Stormwind. The robes are not required for further training, but they show that the Church recognizes you as a servant of the Holy Light.

quest:5634.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, human priests seek a prayer for their own hour of need. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena teaches acolytes to call on the Holy Light when their lives are at risk. Priests in the Cathedral of Light learn to use their faith to shield companions, heal wounds, and strike at evil. Yet even the devout can be isolated, cornered, or brought close to death. In such moments, an acolyte may cry out to the Holy Light for help, with their own survival at stake. High Priestess Laurena guides clergy in Stormwind's Cathedral Square and judges when an acolyte is ready for deeper teachings. Human initiates who show devotion to the Light across the kingdom receive this lesson as both protection and a charge to continue serving the realm.

quest:5635.text: Desperate Prayer. Promising priests from Elwynn Forest are summoned to Stormwind for further training in the Church of the Holy Light. After proving their devotion and discipline, they come before High Priestess Laurena at the Cathedral of Light. Priestess Josetta guides novice priests in Goldshire, while other local mentors serve the outlying settlements of Elwynn Forest. When a disciple proves capable in spirit and deeds, word reaches the senior priesthood in Stormwind. A summons to the Cathedral of Light marks the move to deeper responsibilities in the faith and formal training at the spiritual heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind. At the Cathedral, acolytes present themselves to High Priestess Laurena, one of the Church's senior leaders in Stormwind. She oversees their spiritual grounding and practical training as newly elevated priests. Her instruction prepares them for the harsh trials facing the Alliance and teaches the Light's miracles, including Desperate Prayer, the plea for salvation known among human practitioners.

quest:5637.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, dwarven priests are called to deepen their service to the Light. High Priestess Laurena summons promising acolytes from Dun Morogh to the Cathedral of Light. There they take on wider duties among the Alliance. Dwarven priests trained in Dun Morogh can outgrow the lessons of local mentors like Maxan Anvol in Kharanos. When an acolyte shows promise, High Priestess Laurena sends a formal summons from the Cathedral of Light. Her attention means the young priest is ready for deeper study and greater duties in the faith. Ironforge keeps its own holy traditions in the Mystic Ward, while Stormwind's Church of the Holy Light welcomes humans and dwarves alike. The journey south by Deeprun Tram brings dwarven acolytes into the wider church community and strengthens the spiritual bond between the allied kingdoms.

quest:5638.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, a summons carries a young priest from the Park to the Cathedral of Light. Nara Meideros sends you to High Priestess Laurena for further instruction. In Stormwind’s Park, Nara Meideros keeps faith with Elune. The city’s spiritual guides share ties across their different traditions. When the Cathedral seeks a promising student, Nara sends you across the canals with quiet encouragement. The message brings good tidings, not cause for alarm. At the Cathedral of Light in Cathedral Square, you report to High Priestess Laurena. One of Stormwind’s senior clerical leaders, she guides young acolytes beyond their first prayers. Laurena teaches the sacred invocation called Desperate Prayer, a personal plea for divine aid. It can mend grievous wounds in an instant when a servant of the Light stands near death.

quest:579.text: Stormwind Library. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald copies the kingdom’s histories for those with library scrips. Young King Anduin Wrynn has set aside royal funds for the work, opening these accounts of Azeroth to citizens and scholars. While Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor guide Stormwind’s defenses and court in King Varian’s absence, young King Anduin turns royal support toward learning. He funds copies of ancient manuscripts and historical journals, so the kingdom’s past can be preserved and studied. Within Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library keeps these written accounts and copies them for those in royal service. Hand copying delicate parchment takes time, ink, and royal sanction. Librarian Donyal Tovald accepts official library scrips issued to adventurers and scholars across Alliance territories. In return, he provides copies of historical works, from the ancient histories of the Eastern Kingdoms to accounts of distant lands, offering knowledge of conflicts beyond the capital.

quest:59.text: Cloth and Leather Armor. In Goldshire, Cloth and Leather Armor sends a trusted traveler east for gear. Marshal Dughan issues an armor marker redeemable with Sara Timberlain at Eastvale Logging Camp. The trip carries recruits beyond Guard Thomas's bridge to obtain armor for the realm's defense. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern river crossing, where murlocs and gnolls threaten the border. After you carry his report to Goldshire, Marshal Dughan recognizes your service with an official Stormwind Armor Marker. Goldshire's garrison has meager stores, so Dughan gives you a marker instead of drawing equipment from them. The marker is a military voucher that records your service to the crown. East of Guard Thomas's bridge lies Eastvale Logging Camp, Elwynn's main timber operation. Sara Timberlain works there under an official commission from the Stormwind Army to make cloth and leather gear. The kingdom's central armories are strained, leaving local artisans like Sara to outfit troops and auxiliary scouts on the frontier.

quest:6.text: Bounty on Garrick Padfoot. In Northshire, an Alliance bounty names Garrick Padfoot, a notorious local thief. Deputy Willem at Northshire Abbey calls for recruits to hunt him near the vineyards. Northshire Valley once offered a safe place to train recruits and tend its sacred vineyards. As order falters across Elwynn, thieves have reached the valley. Garrick Padfoot, a cutthroat, quickly rose to lead them. For weeks, he and his gang have plundered shipments, robbed merchants on the roads, and threatened local farmers. Stormwind's guards are stretched thin, protecting the capital and its outer borders. Local marshals and deputies rely on volunteers to keep Northshire peaceful. Deputy Willem places a public bounty on Garrick's head, hoping to rid the valley of his gang. Bringing Padfoot down at his rundown shack east of the river strikes at the lawlessness spreading through the human heartland.

quest:60.text: Kobold Candles. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle seeks candles from kobolds that have overstocked Elwynn Forest's mines. Visiting from his shop in Stormwind, the alchemist needs their thick wax, and the errand introduces adventurers to the subterranean pests encroaching on the kingdom's valuable gold veins.
