William Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary with his brother in Stormwind City's Trade District. Wax is always in short supply as he brews remedies, ointments, and concoctions. Instead of buying polished candles from city merchants, Pestle turns to the vermin in Elwynn. The kobolds carry hefty lumps of tallow and wax on their brows, ready for an adventurer willing to pry them loose. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. These snuffling creatures prize their candles above almost all else. The flickering flames guide them through dark shafts as they dig for gold and shiny trinkets. Taking the candles replenishes Pestle's alchemy stocks and chips away at the vermin choking off the kingdom's precious mining claims.

quest:61.text: Shipment to Stormwind. William Pestle sends a parcel from Goldshire to his brother Morgan in Stormwind. Its candles carry wax supplies from Elwynn Forest to Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. William gathers herbs, reagents, and raw goods in Goldshire, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot easily leave his post at the Lion's Pride Inn, so he depends on travelers heading into the city to carry goods for him. William's parcel holds large candles gathered from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. He says he collects them for their wax. Delivering the shipment brings those supplies to Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District.

quest:62.text: The Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds have overrun The Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure farms. The mine's fall points to a growing pest problem across Elwynn Forest. While Northshire Valley faces its own vermin, reports reach Goldshire that kobolds have claimed another vital site. Between the feuding Stonefield and Maclure homesteads south of town, the Fargodeep Mine once supplied stone and ore for the realm. Now shrill chattering and tallow candles fill its damp tunnels. Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the depths and learn how bad the trouble is. The report of kobolds in the mine adds to the Stormwind Guard's strain. Its troops are already stretched thin defending against Defias bandits and gnoll incursions, leaving too few to clear the tunnels. When Dughan hears the report, he worries about other mineral sites, including the Jasperlode Mine to the northeast.

quest:6261.text: Dungar Longdrink. At Stormwind's Trade District roost, Dungar Longdrink arranges swift gryphon transport for supplies bound to Westfall's embattled defenders. Defias outlaws and feral harvest golems have pushed Westfall close to breaking point. Quartermaster Lewis and the People's Militia are desperate for provisions. Lewis sent word to the capital, and armorer Osric Strang packed the requested equipment. Carrying military cargo on foot through bandit-ridden Elwynn and Westfall takes precious time. Stormwind's new aerial routes offer a vital link to the frontier. The gryphon roost sits in Stormwind's Trade District, where Dungar Longdrink coordinates courier and passenger flights. Wildhammer dwarves traditionally raise and handle these majestic beasts. They carry people and cargo across human lands when roosts at both ends know the route. Bringing Osric's heavy crate straight to Dungar teaches couriers how aerial logistics work. It connects the capital's stockpiles directly to frontier outposts such as Sentinel Hill.

quest:6281.text: Continue to Stormwind. You carry a requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon, where Osric Strang awaits in Old Town. Quartermaster Lewis prepares a requisition note in Sentinel Hill. The local gryphon master Thor offers you the fastest way out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, you ride one of the kingdom's trained gryphons above dusty farmlands and the river border of Elwynn Forest, then over Stormwind City's high white ramparts. After you land at the capital's trade roosts, you head into Old Town to find Osric Strang at his shop, Limited Immunity. Osric supplies the frontier, but his grim reception shows the growing rift between Westfall's beleaguered People's Militia and the distracted rulers in Stormwind Keep.

quest:6285.text: Return to Lewis. Dungar Longdrink sends armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Osric's Crate crosses Elwynn and Westfall by gryphon, carrying supplies to defenders under pressure. Westfall is slipping from the kingdom's grasp. Defias bandits, ravenous gnolls, and mechanical harvest reapers threaten the land. Overland supply routes face harassment, and roads are dangerous for solitary wagons. The flight master network offers a crucial lifeline. Osric, an armorer in Stormwind's Old Town, prepared a heavy crate of armor for the battered volunteers of the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Gryphons are loyal, well-trained beasts, but travel across the lands depends on established familiarity. Dungar Longdrink explains that gryphons instinctively know how to return to their capital roost in Stormwind. To carry a rider to a remote outpost, though, they need the traveler to have met its flight master in person. You have already checked in with Thor at Sentinel Hill, opening the skies over the frontier to rapid travel. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis receives the crate. He is the officer tasked with outfitting Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteer force, and he sets to work distributing the armor among the frontier defenders. For Sentinel Hill, reliable aerial contact with the capital can mean the difference between holding the line and being overrun by the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:64.text: The Forgotten Heirloom. In Westfall, the Furlbrows have fled their farm, leaving a cherished heirloom behind. Recovering the pocket watch offers them a chance to salvage something personal from the chaos spreading through the region. Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna were driven from their Westfall farm by violence. Shouts rose from the pumpkin patches in the night, waking them with little time to gather what they could carry. In the rush to flee, Furlbrow left behind the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. It remains in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse. Defias thugs and thieves, including Benny Blaanco, now pick through the abandoned Furlbrow farm. For ordinary folk, returning for a keepsake could mean death. By securing the pocket watch from the wardrobe, you restore a measure of dignity to a family that has lost nearly everything to Westfall's lawlessness.

quest:65.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's thieves threaten the farms and roads. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you from Sentinel Hill east into Redridge to seek a contact who may know where they hide. Westfall's harvests are gone, and bandits in red bandanas roam the land. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia hold Sentinel Hill under near-constant attack, but they do not know who directs their enemies. Stoutmantle knows that fighting stray looters will not save the region. He needs to find the cartel's inner circle and learn who commands it. Gryan Stoutmantle sets aside military channels and Stormwind's absent nobles, and calls on someone he knows. He sends trusted adventurers east, past Elwynn and into the Redridge Mountains. In Lakeshire, a quiet village by the lake, Wiley the Black waits on the upper floor of the local inn. The rogue knows the underworld better than any militia captain, and may offer the first lead to the Brotherhood's hideouts.

quest:6544.text: Torek's Assault. Torek's Assault is a direct Horde raid launched from the wilds of Ashenvale against the nearby night elf garrison at Silverwing Outpost. Led by the orc raider Torek under orders from Splintertree Post, the strike aims to crush local Sentinel resistance and slay their commander, Duriel Moonfire. It marks one of the most brazen, bloody skirmishes in the ongoing war for Ashenvale's borders. Ashenvale is locked in an escalating border war between the Horde lumber camps and the native night elves. Seeking to break the Alliance's defensive perimeter, Torek gathers a pack of Splintertree raiders just outside Silverwing Outpost. Rather than waiting for a counter-attack, Torek coordinates a head-on charge to shatter the outpost's defenses before the night elves can mount a reinforced campaign against Splintertree Post. Silverwing Outpost stands as a fortified woodland bastion garrisoned by vigilant Silverwing Sentinels and fierce elven warriors. Torek's primary target is their leader, Duriel Moonfire. Bringing down Duriel decapitates the local night elf military hierarchy in the area, allowing the raiders to report a bloody victory back to commander Ertog Ragetusk at Splintertree Post.

quest:6623.text: Horde Trauma. Horde Trauma is a summons directing accomplished Horde medics to report to Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Doctor Gregory Victor, the chief physician of the Horde's trauma division, is looking to recruit and evaluate skilled hands capable of saving lives under extreme pressure. Answering the call places a medic directly into the grim, high-stakes reality of front-line field surgery. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, the orc first aid trainer Arnok delivers word to proficient healers that they have caught the attention of Doctor Gregory Victor himself. Victor oversees Horde Trauma from the fortified outpost of Hammerfall, tucked away in the contested hills of the Arathi Highlands. Arnok views the summons not merely as an order, but as the pinnacle of professional advancement for any battlefield surgeon. Reaching Hammerfall reveals that the post is far from comfortable. Operating amidst constant skirmishes with Stromgarde's forces and local hostile factions, Victor is inundated with wounded grunts, raiders, and scouts. The chief physician wastes no time welcoming newcomers with pleasantries; instead, recruits are immediately ordered into their scrubs to prove their worth during brutal, fast-paced emergency triage.

quest:6641.text: Vorsha the Lasher. Vorsha the Lasher is a violent hydra terrorizing the Horde's foothold at Zoram'gar Outpost along the coast of Ashenvale. Revering the creature's ferocity, the local naga maintain an offering brazier on an offshore island to honor her. By extinguishing this sacred flame, Horde champions provoke Vorsha and draw her ashore to end her predatory assaults. Zoram'gar Outpost sits on a tenuous strip of coast in northwestern Ashenvale, constantly besieged by hostile wildlife, night elves, and serpentine invaders. Among the most destructive threats prowling the Zoram Strand is Vorsha the Lasher, a gargantuan hydra known for brutal, unprovoked strikes against the outpost. The beast emerges from the surf to crush fortifications and butcher warriors before vanishing back into the deep tides. The nearby naga do not merely tolerate the ravenous hydra; they actively venerate her predatory malice. On a rocky outcrop off the strand, the serpentine fiends keep an offering brazier burning continuously in tribute to Vorsha. Muglash, an orc determined to end the constant harassment of the outpost, realized that defiling this ritual flame would bring the beast surging to the surface in a fury, allowing the defenders to lure her into an ambush rather than waiting for another surprise slaughter.

quest:6962.text: Treats for Great-father Winter. Treats for Great-father Winter is a festive holiday request offered during the Feast of Winter Veil in Orgrimmar. The jolly figurehead seated at the Smokywood Pastures display finds himself exhausted after hearing holiday wishes and asks a helpful adventurer for fresh gingerbread cookies and milk. While Greatfather Winter embodies the mythical spirit of winter and abundance across Azeroth, the figure greeting visitors in the Valley of Strength is a hardworking performer employed by Smokywood Pastures. Sitting through long shifts listening to hopeful citizens talk about festive goodies tends to work up an appetite. Tired of simply talking about seasonal treats, the Greatfather gladly enlists passing travelers to satisfy his craving for warm baking and a cold beverage. Satisfying the Greatfather's request requires a touch of home cooking. Adventurers must acquire holiday spices sold directly by the goblin peddlers of Smokywood Pastures, forage small eggs from wild birds across the wilderness, and bake classic gingerbread cookies. Paired with a pitcher of ice cold milk purchased from a local tavern, the modest offering rewards the baker with festive cheer and a small token of gratitude from the feast's organizers.

quest:7.text: Kobold Camp Cleanup. At Northshire, Kobold Camp Cleanup puts new recruits to their first test defending Stormwind's borders. Marshal McBride sends volunteers after kobolds in the northern woods, where their growing numbers threaten the abbey grounds. Northshire Valley once offered quiet for prayer, farming, and novice training. In recent years, Stormwind's forces have grown thin. With the King missing and royal garrisons scattered, wild creatures and opportunists press at civilization's edge. Marshal McBride directs the valley's defense from Northshire Abbey. He depends on fresh volunteers to keep threats from disrupting the abbey or endangering the surrounding vineyards. Kobolds are timid cave-dwellers with a strong attachment to candles. They usually pick at underground seams, far from direct sunlight. Now an entire clan has reached Northshire's northern timberline. If left unchecked, their numbers can turn scavenging into open raids. McBride sends recruits to thin their vanguard and test their resolve to defend the realm.

quest:7025.text: Treats for Greatfather Winter. During the Feast of Winter Veil, the performer portraying Greatfather Winter in Ironforge grows tired and asks passersby for a seasonal treat. Bringing him freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk earns a festive reward and his warm gratitude. While Winter Veil has its roots in ancient titan lore and dwarven myths of an immortal figure cloaked in winter's chill, modern festivities rely heavily on the commercial sponsorship of Smokywood Pastures. Stationed by the holiday tree in the Commons of Ironforge, an ordinary dwarf spends grueling hours suited up as Greatfather Winter, fielding holiday wishes from citizens and eager children alike. After listening to requests for gifts all day, the resident Greatfather Winter inevitably develops a hearty appetite of his own. Rather than asking for something extravagant, he requests a simple comfort: five freshly baked gingerbread cookies made with holiday spices and an ice cold milk to wash them down. The trade offers a moment of relief to an exhausted festival worker and spreads goodwill throughout the snowy capital.

quest:743.text: Dangers of the Windfury. Dangers of the Windfury is a rite of martial readiness offered by Ruul Eagletalon in Bloodhoof Village. Young tauren and Horde adventurers are tasked with battling the savage Windfury harpies nesting in the southeastern cliffs of Mulgore. Hunting these feral predators serves as an essential test of skill and survival before journeying beyond the tribal homeland. In Bloodhoof Village, the veteran warrior Ruul Eagletalon observes all travelers who pass through the heart of Mulgore. For those coming of age or seeking to prove themselves ready for wider adventures, Ruul demands tangible proof of their combat instincts. Survival beyond the sheltered valleys of Mulgore requires poise against aggressive, cunning foes, and Ruul uses the land's fiercest native predators to measure a youth's mettle. The Windfury harpies roost along the mountainous southeastern rim of Mulgore, safely off the beaten trails but constantly posing a threat to wandering wildlife and isolated travelers. Vicious and relentlessly hungry for fresh flesh, these avian terrors rely on swift swoops and razor-sharp claws. Defeating them and claiming their talons demonstrates not only the power to defeat an entrenched threat, but the speed required to counter aerial raiders.

quest:7493.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. "The Journey Has Just Begun" is a Horde quest offered in Orgrimmar to skilled leatherworkers following the defeat of Onyxia. Overlord Runthak recognizes the hero's craft and imparts the rare technique required to fashion protective cloaks from the broodmother's scales. This vital craft prepares the Horde for the deadly flames of Blackrock Spire. The fall of Onyxia represents a triumph for the Horde, but it does not mark the end of the threat posed by the black dragonflight. The broodmother's scaled hide possesses remarkable resilience against draconic flame. Rather than letting such materials go to waste, Horde leadership seeks craftsmen capable of turning the dragon's remains into defensive armor.

quest:7497.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. In Stormwind, Major Mattingly recognizes the artisan who brought down Onyxia. He teaches the craft needed to make a cloak from her scales. Few who helped bring down Onyxia can also work her hide. When an artisan with master leatherworking reports to Major Mattingly in Stormwind, the officer recognizes how much those skills matter in the battles ahead.

quest:76.text: The Jasperlode Mine. Kobolds have overrun the Jasperlode Mine in eastern Elwynn. Marshal Dughan sends scouts to learn how far the infestation has spread. After kobolds swarmed the Fargodeep tunnels south of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan feared they had reached other mines. Jasperlode lies in the rocky foothills northeast of the Tower of Azora and supplies raw stone and metal to the kingdom. Dughan cannot spare Stormwind guards from their town patrols, so he sends independent adventurers east to see whether kobolds have taken this mine too. Scouts who reach Jasperlode's chambers find kobolds have driven out the human miners and fortified the dark passages. Marshal Dughan faces another blow as the crisis grows. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and royal troops are withheld from outlying territories. The local garrison has too few soldiers to clear the mines, leaving the kingdom's heart short of minerals and hemmed in by threats.

quest:768.text: Gathering Leather. Gathering Leather is a straightforward trade request offered by Veren Tallstrider on the rises of Thunder Bluff. To sustain the capital and test young hunters, Veren exchanges a bundle of cured light leather skins for crafted goods. It highlights the deeply ingrained tauren tradition of turning the fruits of the plains hunt into essential clothing and armor. In the newly settled capital atop the high mesas of Mulgore, craftsmanship and survival walk hand in hand. Veren Tallstrider works skins into clothing and protective armor needed by the growing population of Thunder Bluff. Rather than harvesting everything himself, he encourages young adventurers heading out into the plains to bring back their quarry, turning mundane hunting into honorable civic service. For the tauren, hunting beasts across the grasslands is not sport; it is an honorable endeavor that feeds, clothes, and shelters the tribe. Veren Tallstrider looks for hunters with a hunger to bring honor to their clan, asking specifically for light leather stripped from the local wildlife. In return for twelve well-kept hides, he repays the hunter with sturdy goods, reinforcing the mutual support that binds tauren society together.

quest:769.text: Kodo Hide Bag. Kodo Hide Bag is a trade quest offered by Veren Tallstrider, a skilled tauren leatherworker atop the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. In exchange for fundamental crafting supplies, he passes on the traditional plains technique for stitching durable travel packs from sturdy beast hide. It serves as an early rite of passage for apprentice leathercrafters in Mulgore. Perched on Thunder Bluff's crafting rises, Veren Tallstrider upholds the long-standing nomadic tradition of wasting nothing from the hunt. To earn his tutelage, an aspiring leatherworker must present him with cured light leather and sturdy thread. By demonstrating their competence with foundational materials, apprentices prove they are ready to craft goods worthy of carrying survival gear across Kalimdor's rugged expanses. To the tauren, the kodo beast is an emblem of endurance, strength, and steady resolve. Its thick hide shields against brambles, biting wind, and beast claws alike. Crafting bags and garments from kodo hide is not merely a utilitarian act, but an expression of reverence for the animal that has nourished and carried the Shu'halo through countless generations across the plains of Mulgore.

quest:770.text: The Demon Scarred Cloak. The Demon Scarred Cloak is a ragged pelt recovered from the legendary white wolf Ghost Howl, who roams the grassy plains of Mulgore. Marked by an enduring wound inflicted during past clashes with the Burning Legion, the pelt serves as proof of the beast's release from torment. Bringing it to the elders of Bloodhoof Village brings closure to the story of a tragic local legend. Ghost Howl is an elusive white wolf known across Mulgore for both his ferocity and his sorrowful howl. When slain, the beast leaves behind a pelt that is visibly scarred by foul demonic corruption. These lingering marks date back to the wolf's desperate battles against the invading demons of the Burning Legion, a confrontation that left Ghost Howl wounded in both flesh and spirit long after the Third War came to a close. The tauren of Mulgore maintain a deep respect for the wild beasts of their homeland, revering them as children of the Earth Mother. Presenting the scarred cloak to Skorn Whitecloud in Bloodhoof Village confirms the demise of the tormented predator. Skorn recognizes the immense skill required to track and defeat Ghost Howl, expressing the somber hope that in death, the wolf's tortured spirit has finally attained peace.

quest:7781.text: The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head is bound for Stormwind Keep after his defeat in Blackwing Lair. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives the trophy, a sign that the master of Blackrock Mountain has fallen. The victory is among the Alliance's greatest military triumphs in recent history. Nefarian, brood-master of the Black Dragonflight and ruler of Upper Blackrock Spire, has long threatened the surrounding human kingdoms. His defeat ends his twisted experiments and schemes. Carrying his battle-scarred head back to Stormwind gives proof that the Lord of Blackrock has fallen to the Alliance's greatest heroes. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs the kingdom from the throne room of Stormwind Keep. The dragon's severed head shocks the royal court and commands reverence. With the kingdom strained by internal political strife and threats from beyond, the victory lifts morale and earns a place in Alliance history.

quest:783.text: A Threat Within. Volunteers are answering Stormwind's call in Northshire Valley, where local defenses need help. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride explains that the kingdom's forces are spread thin abroad, leaving garrisons short-handed against trouble at home. Northshire Valley once offered quiet for prayer, farming, and monastic study. Now it is Elwynn Forest's first line of defense against unrest at home. Stormwind's regular forces serve on distant fronts, leaving the heartlands short of soldiers. With few guards nearby, the Stormwind Guard must call on every willing volunteer who reaches the abbey. Marshal McBride directs Northshire Valley's defenses from Northshire Abbey as pressures grow. Distant dangers threaten the Alliance, while bandits, vermin, and pests from below ground take advantage of the shortage of soldiers close to home. You answer the call to serve in the valley, starting with the ground around the abbey as threats spread across Elwynn.

quest:83.text: Red Linen Goods. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain needs cloth for her tailoring. She asks passing adventurers to hunt Defias bandits and take their linen bandanas, then uses the cloth to make goods for travelers. Defias bandits across Elwynn wear red linen bandanas. Their less organized kin in Northshire Valley make do with cheap burlap masks. For local craftsmen short on materials, the bandanas offer cloth they can use. Sara Timberlain works as a seamstress at Eastvale Logging Camp, near Elwynn's eastern border. She needs workable textiles for her trade, so she asks adventurers to thin the Defias camps scattered through the woods. The cloth keeps her tailoring supplied while the bandits' encroachment on the area is checked.

quest:8311.text: Hallow's End Treats for Jesper!. Jesper lies sick in Stormwind during Hallow's End, longing for the treats and fun beyond the orphanage. Too ill to go out, he asks Alliance adventurers to gather sweets for him. Jesper stays in the orphanage in Stormwind's Cathedral Square, sick during Hallow's End. He cannot enjoy the childhood pleasure of gathering sweets across Azeroth, so he hopes passing adventurers will share the holiday spirit and collect treats for him. To bring Jesper the sweets he hopes for, you travel beyond Elwynn Forest. You visit the innkeepers of Stormwind, Ironforge, and Darnassus, along with the gnome exile Talvash del Kissel. Each asks you to perform before giving you a treat. You cluck like a chicken, dance, flex, or chug like a train, earning regional sweets such as Stormwind Nougat and Gnomeregan Gumdrops.

quest:8354.text: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. During the festive season of Hallow's End, Innkeeper Norman of the Undercity offers a piece of candy to travelers helping an ailing child. To earn the Undercity Mint, adventurers must cast aside their dignity and flap about like a chicken. The Undercity is rarely known for laughter or warmth, built as it is beneath the ruins of Lordaeron by the liberated Forsaken. Yet when Hallow's End arrives, even the grim denizens of the Trade Quarter join in seasonal revelry. Innkeeper Norman holds onto a stash of Undercity Mints, designated for those collecting treats on behalf of young Spoops, a sick orphan in need of holiday cheer. Rather than surrendering the treat outright to seasoned adventurers, Norman demands a bit of humiliating spectacle. Believing that grown warriors and spellcasters ought to earn their confections, he refuses to part with the mint until the petitioner mimics a barnyard chicken right before his counter.

quest:8356.text: Flexing for Nougat. During autumn's Hallow's End, you gather festive sweets for an orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Allison at the Gilded Rose asks you to flex before she gives you Stormwind Nougat. Hallow's End brings a lighter mood to Stormwind's streets. The holiday marks the turning of the seasons and wards off dark spirits. Common folk celebrate with disguises, revelry, and trick-or-treating. Alliance innkeepers join in, offering traditional sweets to those who perform a harmless trick. At the Gilded Rose in the Trade District, Innkeeper Allison asks for a show before handing out holiday candy, even when you're gathering sweets for Jesper, an orphaned boy. She comments playfully on your physique and asks you to flex your muscles. When you do, she gives you a piece of chewy Stormwind Nougat.

quest:8359.text: Flexing for Nougat. During the festive autumn celebration of Hallow's End, Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar offers sweet seasonal confections to those willing to play along. To earn a piece of Orgrimmar Nougat for a bedridden child, champions of the Horde must swallow their warrior pride and show off their muscles on command. Hallow's End brings high spirits, pranks, and confection gathering to the bustling capitals of Azeroth. While adventuring heroes often face dragons and dark sorcery, the traditions of the autumn holiday require a much lighter touch. Innkeeper Gryshka, presiding over the common room of Orgrimmar's inn, is happy to share her supply of holiday sweets, but only if patrons adhere to the oldest rule of the season: perform a trick, or leave empty-handed. Taking amusement in whatever disguise or armor an adventurer arrives in, Gryshka demands a show of raw Orcish strength. Before parting with a single piece of Orgrimmar Nougat meant for young Spoops, she insists on seeing the mighty traveler strike a muscular pose. It is a lighthearted reminder that even the most feared combatants in the Horde can be made to entertain the common folk for candy.

quest:84.text: Back to Billy. You carry Bernice Stonefield's freshly baked pie across the road to Billy Maclure, who has information about her missing necklace. The delivery continues the feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families in central Elwynn Forest. The old feud between the Stonefields and Maclures leaves little room for kindness. Auntie Bernice Stonefield baked a pork belly pie because Billy Maclure would not share what he knew about her family heirloom without it. She hands you the pie with plain irritation and hopes Billy chokes on every bite.

quest:85.text: Lost Necklace. In southern Elwynn, Bernice Stonefield searches for her missing necklace. She suspects Billy Maclure, the young son of the neighboring family, and asks you to find him across the road. The Stonefield and Maclure families live on adjoining land in southern Elwynn Forest, but they share little goodwill. When "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield discovers her cherished necklace is gone, she blames the youngest Maclure. Certain that Billy Maclure slipped onto her farm and took it, the bitter widow asks you to cross the road to the vineyards, find the boy, and demand its return.

quest:8569.text: Past Efforts in Warsong Gulch. In Warsong Gulch, soldiers fight for Ashenvale while commanders honor their sacrifices. Capital officers accept the Ribbon of Sacrifice as a sign of steadfast service, even when battles bring no clear victory. The Silverwing Sentinels and Warsong Outriders fight brutal skirmishes along Ashenvale’s southern border. Many battles end without a clear victory. Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and other capitals honor those who hold their ground despite the odds. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks fighters who gave themselves to the struggle. Far from the front, Alliance Brigadier Generals and Horde Warbringers oversee their forces. Recruiters send new fighters to Warsong Gulch, while quartermasters and tacticians account for veterans returning from hard campaigns. By honoring courage in stalemate or defeat, their leaders help keep soldiers committed to holding Ashenvale.

quest:86.text: Pie for Billy. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has left Billy Maclure bargaining for a pork belly pie. The Stonefield and Maclure families have feuded for generations, and Billy will say who has the necklace only after he gets his pie. Billy Maclure gives no apology when asked about Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace. He will not return it or say who has it until he gets a freshly baked pork belly pie. He knows Bernice is the finest cook in the valley, and he means to enjoy the bargain. The Maclures and Stonefields have traded insults, brawls, and accusations across their pumpkin patches for generations. Bernice is furious at the thought of feeding the boy she believes stole her family's jewelry, yet she agrees to bake. You gather tender meat from the wild boars roaming the nearby pastures, and she sets aside her pride to get her prized necklace back.

quest:8642.text: Silvervein the Elder. Silvervein the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival atop the hills overlooking Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Travelers pay their respects to him to honor the ancient ties among Azeroth's elder peoples. In return for acknowledging his presence and heritage, he bestows his ancestral blessing. Perched on the rolling ridges above Thelsamar, Elder Silvervein stands as a quiet guardian and reminder of antiquity. As a figure honored during the Lunar Festival, he represents the enduring memories of bygone eras. Even as the surrounding lands of Loch Modan grapple with trogg invasions and local disputes, Silvervein watches peacefully from his overlook. The presence of spirits like Silvervein serves to bridge the divide between modern folk and ancient lineages. When adventurers seek him out, he expresses gratitude that travelers still pay homage to the olden races of Azeroth. His greeting carries the warmth of ancestral appreciation, offering a commemorative token to those who honor him.

quest:8646.text: Hammershout the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Hammershout the Elder appears in Stormwind's Park. Travelers honor the old races and receive a ceremonial token from him. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestor spirits appear across Azeroth with wisdom and blessings for travelers who pay their respects. Hammershout the Elder appears in Stormwind's Park district. His presence near the heart of human civilization recalls the ancient races who walked the land before today's kingdoms rose. Hammershout the Elder asks for no trial or oath, only acknowledgment of the past. He is relieved and grateful when people still honor the old races. In return, he gives travelers a ceremonial token, a sign of the bond between the living and the spirits who came before.

quest:8648.text: Darkcore the Elder. Darkcore the Elder is a seasonal quest encountered during the Lunar Festival within the Undercity. By seeking out Elder Darkcore, travelers pay homage to the ancient spirits honored across Azeroth and receive a Coin of Ancestry in return. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient night elven and earthen ancestors appear throughout the continents to share their wisdom and blessings. Elder Darkcore resides in the shadowed halls of the Undercity, bearing witness to the modern realm while offering remembrance to those who seek out the roots of the world. Approaching Elder Darkcore satisfies an ancient custom of showing respect to the venerable dead and the timeless wardens of Azeroth. In recognition of this pilgrimage, the spirit gifts travelers a Coin of Ancestry as a token of goodwill and enduring memory.

quest:8649.text: Stormbrow the Elder. Near Goldshire, Stormbrow the Elder waits beside the water during the Lunar Festival. Travelers honor ancient traditions and the olden races of Azeroth, and receive a token of remembrance in return. A quiet pond lies just behind the smithy in Goldshire, where Stormbrow the Elder appears. Guards, tradesfolk, and weary travelers pass through town on their way into the forest. Beneath Elwynn Forest's canopy, the honored spirit welcomes anyone who comes to honor the realm's long history. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of great ancestors return to walk among the living. Stormbrow the Elder commends travelers who remember those who came before. For honoring the wisdom and legacy of the elder peoples, he grants a blessing and a commemorative coin for the season.

quest:8652.text: Graveborn the Elder. Graveborn the Elder is a Lunar Festival encounter situated near the town of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. During the celebration, travelers seek out Elder Graveborn among the blighted groves to honor the ancient forebears of Azeroth. Paying respects to this spirit earns his blessing and a token of the holiday. While the Forsaken dwell among ruined manors and grave sites in Tirisfal Glades, the Lunar Festival brings an unexpected communion with ancient times. Elder Graveborn appears as a spectral elder stationed just outside Brill. Even in a realm shattered by the Scourge and reclaimed by the undead, he welcomes pilgrims who pause to honor the ancient ways. The Lunar Festival marks a time when the great spirits of long-past eras return to offer wisdom and gratitude. When travelers approach Elder Graveborn, he remarks on how heartening it is that the inhabitants of Tirisfal still offer homage to the ancestors despite the land's current decay, bestowing a Coin of Ancestry upon those who greet him.

quest:8653.text: Goldwell the Elder. Goldwell the Elder is a Lunar Festival quest offered by Elder Goldwell in Kharanos, Dun Morogh. Honoring him reflects the enduring tradition of seeking out ancestral spirits across the snowbound dwarven lands. In exchange for your respects, he bestows a token of ancestral blessing. Standing in the bitter cold beside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Elder Goldwell watches over the bustling trade path leading to the gates of Ironforge. During the Lunar Festival, this venerable figure welcomes weary travelers, adventurers, and locals alike, embodying the long memory of ancient days when early mortals walked beneath the stars of Azeroth. Approaching Goldwell offers a moment of reflection amidst the harsh winter winds of Dun Morogh. He expresses relief and joy that mortals still remember the ancient races and their deeds, thanking all who pause their journeys to show respect. In turn, he awards a sacred Coin of Ancestry as an emblem of his blessing.

quest:8670.text: Runetotem the Elder. Runetotem the Elder is an encounter with an ancestral spirit during the Lunar Festival in Durotar. Found standing within Razor Hill under a pillar of heavenly light, she offers blessings and festival tokens to travelers who come to pay their respects to the past. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient elders materialize across Azeroth to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem manifests inside Razor Hill, positioned just past the southern entrance. Bathed in a clear beam of starlight from above, she watches over the orcish settlement and welcomes adventurers who step aside from their travels to acknowledge the wisdom of those who came before. Approaching Elder Runetotem does more than honor an individual ancestor. In exchange for your homage, she rewards you with a festival token of fortune and shares word of where other spirits may be found, pointing wanderers toward Elder Darkhorn and Elder High Mountain across the continent.

quest:8673.text: Bloodhoof the Elder. Bloodhoof the Elder is an encounter with one of the venerated ancestral spirits who manifests during the Lunar Festival. Located just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, this honored spirit acknowledges the respect paid by wandering travelers and grants an ancestral token in return. During the celebration of the Lunar Festival, the spirits of great heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Shrouded in celestial radiance, Elder Bloodhoof appears just north of Bloodhoof Village near the bridge. Approaching these venerated ancestors is an act of honoring past sacrifices, and in exchange, Elder Bloodhoof offers words of encouragement and a sacred Coin of Ancestry. Standing on the ancestral lands of Mulgore, Elder Bloodhoof serves as a bridge between the living tauren tribes and the memory of their forebears. For the tauren, honoring the dead is a pillar of spiritual life, reinforcing the harmony between the Earth Mother, the ancestors, and those currently walking the plains.

quest:8675.text: Skychaser the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Skychaser the Elder appears atop Sentinel Tower in Westfall. Travelers climb to honor her and receive her blessing in return. Sentinel Hill holds against Defias raiders and roving scavengers in Westfall's troubled scrublands. During the Lunar Festival, an ancestral spirit named Elder Skychaser appears on the open platform atop Sentinel Tower. From above the dust and wind, she watches over the weary soldiers and beleaguered settlers below. Anyone may climb the tower and pay her respect. Across Azeroth, the Lunar Festival honors wisdom, heritage, and the deeds of ancient spirits who walked the earth before today's struggles. When you approach, Elder Skychaser recognizes the living spark within you. She accepts your homage and gives you a token of her favor, a bond between the living and the honored dead.

quest:8677.text: Darkhorn the Elder. Darkhorn the Elder is a seasonal quest completed by seeking out Elder Darkhorn in Orgrimmar during the Lunar Festival. Travelers pay their respects to the honored ancestor, receiving a token of wisdom and celebration in return. She stands in the heart of the Horde capital as a testament to age, survival, and ancestral pride. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of revered ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with the living. Elder Darkhorn rests within the fortified ramparts of Orgrimmar, observing the bustle of the young warrior city. Approaching her offers champions of the Horde—and any Alliance adventurer brave enough to slip through the gates—a chance to pay formal homage to those who walked the earth generations before. Upon receiving greeting and reverence from passing travelers, Elder Darkhorn acknowledges the vibrant spark of life within them. In exchange for honoring the ways of old, she grants a Coin of Ancestry and her personal blessing. These tokens celebrate the triumph over ancient perils and remind the living to cherish the strength passed down through unbroken bloodlines.

quest:8678.text: Proudhorn the Elder. Proudhorn the Elder is an ancestral tauren spirit honored during the Lunar Festival atop the heights of Thunder Bluff. Visiting him is an act of deep reverence, acknowledging the wisdom of the ancestors who watch over Mulgore and the Horde. Perched high on the windblown mesas of Thunder Bluff, Proudhorn the Elder manifests as an ancestral presence during the Lunar Festival. Tauren culture holds the voices of their ancestors in the highest regard, believing that the spirits of ancient leaders and sages linger to offer guidance and strength to the living. Travelers who climb the heights to pay their respects to Elder Proudhorn are greeted not as strangers, but as vital flames of life. In exchange for the traveler's homage, the elder bestows a Coin of Ancestry, symbolizing communion between the enduring past and the living champions fighting for the world's future.

quest:8680.text: Windtotem the Elder. Elder Windtotem is an honored ancestor spirit who appears on a bluff overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet during the Lunar Festival. Bathed in a radiant shaft of celestial light, she receives travelers seeking to honor the wisdom of ages past. Paying homage to her rewards mortals with an ancestral blessing and guidance toward other elders walking Kalimdor. Perched on a grassy hill just northwest of the flight master in Ratchet, Elder Windtotem looks out over the bustling goblin docks and the open sea. While the harbor beneath her trades in iron, gunpowder, and coin, the elder stands apart in quiet contemplation, touched only by the quiet winds of the Barrens and the celestial glow descending from above. Like the other ancestral spirits summoned forth during the Lunar Festival, Elder Windtotem acts as a guide to wandering mortals. Those who seek her out not only earn her blessing and a token of her favor, but also receive whispers detailing the whereabouts of neighboring elders throughout the continent, including Elder Runetotem and Elder Bloodhoof.

quest:87.text: Goldtooth. Near Fargodeep Mine, Auntie Bernice Stonefield's necklace is missing, and the Stonefield and Maclure families blame each other. Billy Maclure admits he lost it while playing nearby, and you follow the trail to the kobold Goldtooth. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has stirred up trouble between the Stonefield and Maclure families. Bernice suspects her rivals, but Billy Maclure lost the trinket while playing near Fargodeep Mine. He tries to hide his guilt, saying he only found the necklace before a creature snatched it away. Billy says a large kobold with gleaming fangs took the shiny necklace and ran to a den above Fargodeep Mine. Goldtooth actually lurks on the mine's lower level. Slaying the kobold brings Bernice's necklace back, settles the families' dispute, and earns you an old campaign keepsake left by Bernice's late husband.

quest:8717.text: Moonwarden the Elder. Elder Moonwarden is an honored ancestral spirit visited during the Lunar Festival, standing under a celestial beam of light at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Speaking with him offers travelers ancient wisdom and guidance toward other elders scattered throughout the continent. Standing amidst the dusty thoroughfare of the Crossroads, Elder Moonwarden appears bathed in a radiant column of heavenly light. He represents the ancient spirits revered during the Lunar Festival, a time when mortals pause their conflicts to pay homage to the wisdom of past generations. Elder Moonwarden muses on the starry heavens and their ability to reveal earthly mysteries to those who look up in search of truth. In addition to bestowing his own ancestral blessings, he offers seekers direction toward fellow elders across Kalimdor, including Elder Bloodhoof, Elder High Mountain, Elder Morningdew, and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8718.text: Bladeswift the Elder. Elder Bladeswift is an ancestral spirit honored during the Lunar Festival within the night elven capital of Darnassus. Located in the Cenarion Enclave, this ancient figure offers travelers wisdom drawn from the starry heavens above. Seeking his blessing connects adventurers directly to the revered traditions of the Cenarion Circle and the night elven people. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of revered ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom and bestow blessings upon travelers. Bladeswift the Elder stands amidst the serene boughs of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Unlike modern residents preoccupied with the trials of the present, this spectral forebear looks upward to the cosmos, contemplating the mysteries woven into the night sky. Night elven culture has long revered the celestial bodies as reflections of Elune and the deeper secrets of existence. Bladeswift reminds those who approach him that the countless stars hold answers to worldly struggles, urging the wise and fortunate to gaze upward. By acknowledging his presence, adventurers receive a Coin of Ancestry and take part in a timeless ceremony bridging the mortal realm with the spirits of the past.

quest:8721.text: Starweave the Elder. Starweave the Elder is a Lunar Festival quest encountered in Darkshore. Adventurers seek out Elder Starweave in the settlement of Auberdine to pay their respects to the ancestral spirits of Kalimdor. In exchange for honoring ancient traditions, she offers celestial wisdom and her blessing. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of venerated ancestors manifest across the continents of Azeroth, battened in pillars of radiant celestial radiance. Elder Starweave takes her place among the night elves of Auberdine, a critical harbor town situated along the mist-shrouded coast of Darkshore. Travelers honoring the festival make pilgrimage to her side, seeking the timeless guidance of ages past. Elder Starweave contemplates the cosmic tapestry above Kalimdor, reminding all who approach that the stars carry answers to mortal doubts and worldly riddles. Those who take the time to seek her council are urged to look skyward for truth and receive ancestral favor alongside tidings of other wandering spirits across the wild frontier.

quest:8725.text: Riversong the Elder. Elder Riversong is an ancestral night elf spirit honored during the Lunar Festival, found resting beneath a quiet shrine in Astranaar. Bathed in a beam of moonlight, she offers quiet wisdom to travelers and directs pilgrims toward other revered ancestors across the lands of Kalimdor. Amid the ancient boughs and wooden walkways of Astranaar, Elder Riversong appears under an open night elf shrine. Marked by a distinct column of celestial light piercing the Ashenvale canopy, her ethereal presence serves as a focal point for participants in the Lunar Festival seeking communion with past generations. Elder Riversong reminds pilgrims of the ancient night elven tradition of reading truth and mystery in the starry sky. Her words direct travelers to seek wisdom through patience and contemplation, guiding those honoring the season on toward fellow spirits, including Elder Starweave.

quest:88.text: Princess Must Die!. At Stonefield Farm, Ma Stonefield wants Princess Must Die! before Princess ruins the harvest. The enormous prize-winning sow from Brackwell Pumpkin Patch keeps raiding the Stonefields’ vegetables, and Ma wants the family to gather their crops in peace. Princess has put the Stonefield harvest at risk. The prize-winning sow belongs to the Brackwells, but she has grown enormous by crossing onto the Stonefield plots and devouring their vegetables. Ma Stonefield has had enough of the sow eating the crops she worked to grow. She wants Princess put down before the pig ruins the season’s yield. Princess does not roam alone. At Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, east beyond the Maclure homestead, protective boars surround her. To prove the sow will trouble the Stonefield fields no more, you need to get past her guards and bring back the distinctive brass collar from her neck.

quest:8828.text: Winter's Presents. Winter's Presents is an invitation extended to adventurers in Orgrimmar during the Feast of Winter Veil. Guided by holiday organizers and goblin apparatus tenders, Horde heroes are directed to visit Great-father Winter beneath the decorated festive tree to claim gifts prepared for them. As the chill winds of late year sweep across Durotar, the Feast of Winter Veil brings a rare moment of peace and celebration to the harsh red stones of Orgrimmar. Promoters from Smokywood Pastures, alongside holiday enthusiasts, ensure that every warrior, hunter, and wanderer resting in the capital knows that gifts await them beneath the decorated tree. Seated amidst holiday ribbons and packaged cartons near the Smokywood Pastures market stands Great-father Winter himself. While the ancient figure embodies the renewal of the season, the savvy merchant goblins never miss an opportunity to remind visitors that the holiday spirit pairs exceptionally well with their stock of seasonal wares and festive treats.

quest:8866.text: Bronzebeard the Elder. Bronzebeard the Elder is a Lunar Festival encounter with Elder Bronzebeard within the dwarven mountain city of Ironforge. Honoring him during this ancestral celebration rewards travelers with wisdom and a token of his esteem. It reflects the deep reverence the folk of Khaz Modan hold for their forebears and long-lived heritage. During the Lunar Festival, spirits and venerable elders manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with travelers honoring the past. In Ironforge, Elder Bronzebeard stands as an embodiment of the stalwart resilience of the Bronzebeard clan. When approached by adventurers seeking to pay their respects, he expresses quiet satisfaction that the people of this land still acknowledge and honor the lineage of the olden races. The encounter requires no great trial or perilous expedition, asking only that travelers pause, acknowledge the elder's presence, and offer greeting. In turn, Elder Bronzebeard extends his well wishes and bestows a Coin of Ancestry. These sacred festival tokens serve as physical reminders of the living connection between modern heroes and the generations who forged Khaz Modan from stone and fire.

quest:92124.text: Book Inventory. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton is frustrated by misplaced and missing tomes. He asks young adventurers to find Daniel, his daydreaming assistant, and take stock of the library archives, but Daniel's thoughts keep wandering to local tradeskills, making a straight answer hard to get. Northshire Abbey preserves old scholarly works, spiritual writings, and historical records that survived the First War in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Brother Paxton, a meticulous monk, takes great pride in the collection. Lately, books have gone missing from the shelves, and Paxton needs a clear inventory to learn how widespread the loss is. He has little patience to chase after his daydreaming helper. Daniel works as Brother Paxton's assistant in the abbey library, but his thoughts rarely stay with parchment and catalog numbers. He is fascinated by the practical trades of Elwynn Forest: smithing, leatherworking, tailoring, and herbal craft. Paxton grows exasperated as inventory work leads Daniel to ramble about local crafters instead of locating lost scriptures.

quest:9260.text: Investigate the Scourge of Stormwind. Scourge forces press against Stormwind, with necropolises looming beyond its walls. Lieutenant Orrin calls defenders to strike their camps, gather Necrotic Stones, and study the runes there. Scourge forces have reached the outskirts of Stormwind City. Necropolises float overhead as undead and cultists take hold near the kingdom’s greatest bastion. Lieutenant Orrin gathers defenders outside the city to drive them back before they threaten the capital. Glowing runes mark the dirt around Scourge camps, and their purpose remains unclear. The circles crackle with magic like that of the necropolises and carry eerie whispers. Lieutenant Orrin can only guess who, if anyone, hears those unnatural voices.

quest:92742.text: Testing the Wells. Alba Fairmoon sends you across Westfall to test the farm wells. The samples may reveal what is poisoning the soil and groundwater. Alba Fairmoon asks you to test Westfall's groundwater. Neglect and banditry have already hurt the open plains, and poison beneath the earth threatens the farmland that remains. You collect samples from farm wells so Alba can learn what is tainting the soil and water. You take samples from the wells at Jansen Stead and Molsen Farm. These homesteads lie among scattered farms exposed to Defias outlaws and feral wildlife. Their well water can show whether the blight is rising from the ground, caused by magic, or deliberately put into the water that feeds the region.

quest:92744.text: Murloc Gills. Alba Fairmoon sends Alliance help to Westfall's Longshore to gather murloc gills. She fears the crop blight may reach the Great Sea, and the gills could reveal whether the coastal waters are tainted. Westfall is already near ruin, with crops failing, farmers displaced, and bandits roaming the roads. Alba Fairmoon fears the blight may be draining from inland fields into the Great Sea. If the coast is tainted, the fish that feed Westfall's poor and grace Stormwind City's tables could vanish. That loss could tip an already strained kingdom into outright famine. Murlocs are stubborn and violent, but their amphibious bodies make them natural signs of water quality. Their breathing constantly filters seawater, leaving their gills exceptionally receptive to poisons, blight, and unnatural pollutants. Alba Fairmoon hopes to gauge the contamination by studying fresh gills from the murlocs prowling the Longshore.

quest:92745.text: The State of the Mines. Alba Fairmoon finds toxic metals in Westfall's wells and fears for its farmland. She suspects the mines seized by the Defias and warns the soil could fail for decades. You head to Jangolode Mine and Gold Coast Quarry to disrupt the mining. Alba Fairmoon finds dangerous levels of toxic metals in Westfall's wells. Once Stormwind's main breadbasket, the region now faces a threat to its crops. Alba suspects the mines seized by the Defias Brotherhood are poisoning the water. If the contamination continues, the surrounding earth could lie barren for decades. The Defias put local creatures to work alongside their highwaymen, stripping Westfall of its resources. Riverpaw gnolls dig for stone and minerals at Gold Coast Quarry, while kobold diggers tunnel through Jangolode Mine. Disrupting their labor weakens the Defias' ability to process and distribute contaminated minerals.

quest:92747.text: Moonbrook Espionage. Alba Fairmoon sends you to scout Moonbrook, where signs of industry trouble the Alliance. The poison found across Westfall does not seem to come from the lesser mines, so attention turns to the Deadmines beneath the town. The mines already examined across Westfall offer no answer to the poison spreading through the region. No known surface excavation appears to be its source. One major site remains unexplored: the vast shafts of the Deadmines, directly beneath Moonbrook’s ruined streets.

quest:92748.text: Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, toxic industry beneath the Deadmines is poisoning the farmland. You travel to Stormwind's Dwarven District to seek an engineer who can supply heavy explosives. Westfall faces displaced vagrants and banditry under the Defias Brotherhood. Evidence from across the region points to a coordinated, mechanised threat underground. Industrial refuse and caustic toxins foul the soil, and their trail leads into the Deadmines, where an organized operation works below the earth. Fortified tunnels and machinery in the Deadmines call for more than ordinary weapons. To stop the poison reaching Westfall's fields, you seek help in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. Roaring forges, tinkerers, and merchants selling blasting powder fill the district. There you look for Sprite Jumpsprocket, an engineer who can devise explosives for the work.

quest:92749.text: A Dynamite Plan. Sprite Jumpsprocket is eager to put dynamite to work in Stormwind. The inventive tinkerer in the Dwarven District has heard talk of industrial sabotage and wants a supply of coarse dynamite to begin her plan. Sprite Jumpsprocket, a gnome engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District, welcomes talk of industrial sabotage. Rather than urge caution, she asks passing mercenaries to bring her a bundle of coarse dynamite. You can make coarse dynamite at an engineering workbench or trade with the city's craftsmen. Sprite asks for ten sticks, enough to disrupt the industrial schemes unfolding in the surrounding territories. Her plan shows the practical, perilous methods gnomes favor when facing mechanical and political disruptions.

quest:92750.text: Detonation at a Distance. Sprite Jumpsprocket needs a safer way to set off explosives, and Stormwind holds the answer. She sends you to Stormwind Intelligence for a remote detonator. Sprite Jumpsprocket wants to set off explosives from a safe distance. Goblins and gnomes are known for handling volatile chemicals recklessly, but some blasts demand care. A standard fuse can put the person lighting it in danger. Sprite knows a controlled explosion needs a special trigger, the kind common tinkerers do not keep on hand. Sprite sends you to Stormwind Intelligence in Old Town instead of to local dwarven blasters or ordinary engineering suppliers. The network is known as SI:7, and its covert agents handle sabotage, stealth, and targeted demolitions. Jasper Fel works among them in the capital and can provide discreet, dangerous equipment.

quest:92751.text: Detonation at a Distance. In Moonbrook, explosions beneath Westfall draw SI:7's attention. Jasper Fel, a Stormwind operative, sends a remote detonator kit to help handle the work from a safe distance. Jasper Fel and SI:7 watch events across Stormwind's lands, including Westfall's troubled border. When word reaches him of explosive work in Moonbrook, Fel already knows what is happening in the abandoned mining tunnels beneath the countryside.

quest:92752.text: Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, Sprite Jumpsprocket sends a volatile charge to Alba Fairmoon. The primed explosives must reach her safely, with the detonator undisturbed. Sprite Jumpsprocket has finished a bundle of Extra-Destructive Explosives for Alba Fairmoon. Carrying a live charge through wartime Westfall adds danger to a road already threatened by Defias bandits and feral beasts. Sprite Jumpsprocket warns you to mind the detonator. The cargo is meant to destroy the hidden industrial operation in the Deadmines, which is poisoning Westfall's farmland. Alba Fairmoon needs the explosives intact before she can use them.

quest:92753.text: Destruction in Deadmines. Deep beneath Moonbrook, Defias industry is poisoning the land. Alba Fairmoon suspects their metallurgical forge is the source of the blight and sends you to destroy it with explosives. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines shelter a fortified complex that powers the Defias Brotherhood. Its heavy forge smelts metal and builds machinery. Alba Fairmoon believes this forge is the likely origin of the contamination blighting the area. Destroying it is her aim.

quest:92819.text: Destruction in Deadmines. In Westfall, Alba Fairmoon sends an operative to destroy the Defias forge in the Deadmines. The explosives are already planted, and Alba waits in the hills behind Moonbrook for the detonator. The Deadmines hold the Defias Brotherhood's strength beneath Westfall. Alba Fairmoon directs you to sabotage the forge hidden in the mines. The explosives are already planted beside it, and you return to Alba in the hills behind Moonbrook to set them off from a safe distance. She hopes destroying the forge will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal. The charge sits beside the forge deep in the Deadmines. A remote detonator lets you set it off from outside the caves, after you rejoin Alba Fairmoon in the hills behind Moonbrook. She hopes that with the forge destroyed, Westfall's poisoned land can begin to heal.

quest:95065.text: Fishin' Time. At Stormwind harbor, Gilbert Gray's bait runs low as the fish begin to bite. He asks passersby to fetch supplies from a shop along the city's canals. Gilbert Gray spends quiet days fishing at the edge of Stormwind harbor. He watches his bobber on the water, but a good run of biting fish can empty his bait tin. With his supplies gone and the fish still biting, the elderly angler asks passersby to bring him more. Catherine Leland runs a tackle shop along the stone canals, just west of the Trade District. She supplies fishermen across Stormwind with lures and bait, including regulars like Gilbert Gray.

quest:96607.text: The Great Outdoors. You learn how rest and preparation help you survive beyond city walls. Travelers across Azeroth teach new wanderers to rest by a campfire and prepare for the wilds. Even a sharp blade or potent magic cannot protect you from the wilds if you neglect the basics of survival. Seasoned wanderers near roadside clearings share this lesson with travelers leaving their home valleys. Resting by a campfire eases sore boots, settles the mind, and readies you for the road ahead. Regular rest and preparation give you a better chance of surviving long enough to find fortune and glory. Once you understand the value of a fire and proper rest, your instructors point you toward town tradesfolk. A field camp needs more than an ember and a bedroll; survival also calls for practical crafts. You can forge replacement rivets, cook trail rations, or stitch torn gear under the stars. Each profession offers camp fixtures that can help turn a bare hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.

quest:96627.text: The Adventurer. In Northshire Valley, Marshal McBride sends The Adventurer toward Goldshire to find Sam Sarsaparilla. You have shown your skill defending the abbey, and McBride wants you to look into the newcomer. As threats from the local Defias and vermin ease, Marshal McBride turns his attention to the road beyond Northshire Valley. Stormwind's regular forces are stretched thin across the kingdom, so the local garrison relies on promising fighters to watch travelers and wanderers in the surrounding woods. Marshal McBride asks you to check on Sam Sarsaparilla, a newcomer spotted near Goldshire. It is an unusual request, not a military order or a bounty hunt, and it leads you from Northshire's secluded valley into the wider wilds of Elwynn Forest.

quest:96658.text: Camping 101: Cooking. At nearby settlements, new adventurers learn to cook and kindle a Basic Campfire for life in the wild. The lesson is offered across Alliance and Horde lands. Every traveler needs to know how to build a fire beyond the safety of fortified walls. A campfire can boil water and roast meat, and it anchors a campsite in unfamiliar country. Apprentice cooks can kindle only modest fires with few surroundings. Greater skill in cooking lets them light larger fires that support more elaborate campsites. Other practical trades also teach ways to make useful furnishings for a camp.

quest:97894.text: Business in Auberdine. Borgus Steelhand seeks news of his brother Gorbold in Auberdine. The dwarven merchant asks travelers sailing west to check on Gorbold, who recently began trading in the night elven port. Their route links Stormwind Harbor with the shores of northern Kalimdor. Borgus Steelhand trusts his family's name among traders. His brother, Gorbold Steelhand, crossed the Great Sea recently to work a merchant stall in Auberdine. Gorbold hoped to profit by supplying ships that call at Darkshore. Weeks have passed without a word, and Borgus worries about how his brother fares so far from Ironforge and Stormwind. Travel from the Eastern Kingdoms to Kalimdor once meant a winding passage through Menethil Harbor or neutral goblin ports such as Booty Bay. Borgus directs travelers to a vessel at the southern-most dock of Stormwind Harbor. It sails directly to Auberdine's long wooden piers.

quest:97914.text: Expanding Horizons. Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine across the Great Sea to Stormwind. The letter asks City Architect Baros Alexston to recognize Auberdine's work and its home. Auberdine now links Darkshore to Stormwind by sea. Night elves once kept to Kalimdor's forests, apart from the Eastern Kingdoms, but after the Third War they joined the Grand Alliance. The new passage gives the northern port a direct tie to the human kingdom. Local leaders want the shipping route secured and Auberdine connected to the wider Alliance. Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, ruined cities nearby, have long drawn more notice than the living coastal settlement. The letter crossing the Great Sea is addressed to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect. He oversees construction and infrastructure in the human capital, including public works and logistics. Thundris Windweaver wants Auberdine's work recognized and its home made known.

quest:97919.text: Camping 101: First Aid. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Michelle Belle shows travelers how to prepare for camp. In Goldshire, you can learn to make a First Aid Kit for the road ahead. Travel across Elwynn Forest can leave you wounded, far from a town healer or inn. First Aid lets you tend your own injuries and care for yourself without relying on others. Bandages offer help with bleeding and trauma, without arcane rituals or holy supplication. A campsite offers a place to rest amid the dangers of the wild. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Michelle Belle teaches skilled practitioners to assemble First Aid Kits. Keep medical supplies at camp so a weary party can treat injuries and regain strength before facing the perils ahead.

quest:97920.text: Camping 101: Fishing. In Elwynn Forest, novice anglers seek ways to make camp life more comfortable. Near Goldshire, fishing expert Lee Brown teaches travelers how angling can add simple comforts to a campsite. Fishing gives you food, but camp life asks for more than food and shelter. A fish bowl can bring comfort and lift the spirits of weary travelers between excursions. Sound minds and high spirits help make formidable fighters. Lee Brown waits beside the waters outside Goldshire to help novice fishermen broaden their craft. Travelers who show skill with rod and line can learn how simple catches and basic materials become useful additions to a campsite.

quest:98247.text: Shipping Label. The Shipping Label is a recovered freight marker attached to a supply crate owned by the Azeroth Commerce Authority. Directing couriers to their trade hub at the Three Corners crossroads in Redridge Mountains, it introduces travelers to the organization's network of independent haulers. Found pasted to a stocked supply crate, this damaged shipping label marks cargo belonging to the Azeroth Commerce Authority. Although the intended destination and recipient have been torn away, clear instructions direct anyone who discovers the freight to return it or report to the authority's trade outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Beside the formal text, a rudimentary map sketches out the roads leading toward the Three Corners intersection. At the crossroads of Three Corners, representatives of the Azeroth Commerce Authority actively enlist travelers as independent couriers. Rather than binding haulers to strict merchant contracts, the authority operates an informal network where adventurers are compensated with Merchant's Favor in return for recovering missing cargo and fulfilling abandoned deliveries along the highway.
